notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0180a.stoa002.opp-l: 1.1: The biblical quotation contains a Greek word, ἐξνήλωσα, evidently for ἐξανήλωσα 'I consumed'; translated so. 'dari in uobis benedictionem' is awkward Latin; rendered as purpose ('so that a blessing may be given'). 3.1: Many evident scanning errors corrected silently (e.g. 'ei neglexerunt' for 'et', 'dc anathemate' for 'de', 'do. mino' for 'domino', 'dem' for 'deum', 'interfiei' for 'interfici', 'm celabis' for 'nec celabis', 'crunt' for 'erunt', 'facio anathema' for 'factus anathema'). 'ualle le Achar' read as 'uallem Achar'. 'Iambri' (the Old Latin form) rendered with the Hebrew name Zabdi; 'Mecachor' taken as Emek Achor (the Valley of Achor). 'quas sis in aeternum daturus poenas' is loosely joined to its sentence and may be corrupt. The edition's '(quod)' is supplied, translated as [and].

Line 5.1 contains intruded critical apparatus from the printed page ('2 dei v 15 fuit v, fuerit V ... idololatram v'); it has been omitted. It records the editor's readings 'haec te dicimus', 'es', 'seu', which the text already follows. 'nobis nescire deum' read as 'uobis'. 'nonas uias' read as 'nouas'. In the Amaziah quotation 'insurrexerunt ad eum insurrexerunt' appears corrupt (a noun such as 'insidiatores' may be lost), and 'inter fecerunt #** eum in equis' is garbled (cf. 2 Chron. 25:27-28: they killed him there and brought him back on horses); marked [...]. 'illius clementiae' (5.1 end of 4.1) taken as a title for God. The prophet's name 'Baneas' is not in the Hebrew text of 2 Chron. 25 and is kept as given.

Line 2 quotes an Old Latin version of 4 Kings (2 Kings) 22–23 that is badly garbled in this edition: names (Alchinae, Achiliae, Acican, Tacuelarum, Agabae, Basabe, Phem, Cepenan, Faradin, Amissa, Gamos, Mulcro) have been rendered by their evident biblical identifications (Ahikam, Achbor, Tikvah, Geba, Beersheba, Topheth, Hinnom, precincts/parvarim, Mount of Corruption, Chemosh, Milcom). The text marked '**#' before 'posuerant reges' is lacunose; '[And he took away the horses which]' is supplied from the biblical sense. 'quos posuit tres equos' and 'fontem solis' (for currum solis, chariot of the sun) are corrupt; translated by sense. 'uidebunt oculi tui' lacks the negative required by the sense; 'not' supplied. 'extraxit filios' read as pulling down houses (domos) per the biblical text. In line 1, 'altare' in Uzziah's hand presumably means a censer. 'non erit tibi bonum, ut ... ordines' is elliptical.

Line 8.1: 'pastor eram caprarum uellicans' – the object of 'plucking' (sycamore figs in Amos 7:14) is lacking in this text; supplied in brackets. 'Arcedonossar' is taken as Esarhaddon (Sacherdonos in the Greek Tobit). 'tollo illum de platea ita unum locum apud me' seems corrupt (perhaps 'in unum locum'); translated by sense. Line 9.1: 'noluit' ('he did not will') in 'per quos omnia praecepta sua noluit ... perferri' makes no sense in context; read as 'uoluit'. 'effuriabuntur' taken as 'they will rage'; 'domus amaricans' rendered 'embittering house'.

Line 1: 'facis est' read as 'factum est'. In Judith's prayer several phrases follow the Old Latin closely and are obscure ('in principe et principem super seruum suum'; 'in uulnere et in liuorem'); rendered literally. Line 3: in the 1 Maccabees quotation, 'et in domos eorum' and 'et eos qui circumciderant eos' lack verbs; '[plundered]' and '[killed]' supplied from the sense of the Greek. 'celatus est' read as 'zelatus est'; 'attulit' marked with a sign in the edition. 'statuens testamentum. mentum' is a dittography; 'in mentum' read as 'in montes' (into the mountains). 'Iambrim filio Salom' is Zimri son of Salu (Num. 25), rendered from the text's form as Zambri son of Salom.

13.1: 'regis edicto quam dei temperasse' read as '[magis] regis edicto quam dei' (complied with the king's edict rather than God's). 'illi te gladio fuerant interfectori' appears corrupt (perhaps 'interfecturi') and repeats the preceding clause. 'cur non satis agens?' is obscure; rendered 'Why are you not taking action?'. 'Isw' read as Isaac. 14.1: 'antichristus gentes' read as 'aduersus gentes'; 'utros' as 'uiros'; 'derunt' as 'dederunt'; 'dem:)' as 'deus'. 'et percusserunt uirtutem' seems corrupt (1 Macc 2:44 has 'they gathered an army'); rendered 'they mustered a force'. The words quoted from 'the second book of Ezra' (= Nehemiah) are Nehemiah's; '[Nehemiah]' is supplied for the speaker, whom the Latin leaves unnamed. 15.1: 'alii habe certum quod deum' read as 'aut habe certum quod deus'; 'nount' as 'nonne'; 'gelum' as 'zelum'. 'sibi traditis' (concerning those handed over to them) is uncertain.

Line 16.1: 'in legum resurrectionem' is read as 'in Iesum resurrectionem' (Acts 4:2); 'timebant ... ne laudarentur' in 17.1 is read as 'ne lapidarentur' (stoned), per Acts 5:26. Line 17.1: 'sibi delegatum totidem etiam dei populum' appears corrupt; translated as 'what had been entrusted to them; and likewise that the people of God'. Other evident scanning errors (e.g. 'in possumus' for 'non possumus', 'ulti' for 'ulli', 'inmni-entes' for 'inuenientes', 'contua meliosi' for 'contumeliosi') silently corrected. 'Concarnificis tui' (your fellow-executioner) refers to Antiochus.

'conseotinum'/'conscotinum' read as 'conscotinum', 'fellow-Scotinus': Lucifer's pun on Photinus ('the enlightened') as Scotinus ('the dark'), hence 'reversing the sense'. The Greek letters in the scan are read as homoousion. In the parable of the talents, the text mixes 'talentum' and 'mna' as given. 'sed aequitatem custodire' after the Timothy quotation is unclear and possibly corrupt; translated tentatively. Several minor scanning errors corrected silently, among them 'ingentibus', 'discrimine', 'uolt', 'perficientes' and 'ciuitates'.

20.1: 'quo tecum conlido agentes' is obscure, perhaps corrupt (confido? colloquio?); rendered by sense as 'dealing with you in this manner'. 'Bariesuban ... quod interpretatur Paratus' and 'Etoemus' (for Elymas/Etoimas) follow this text's biblical version. 'credimus hoc instructum testimonio. non te dicturum' taken as one sentence. 22.1: several evident scanning errors read as intended (aspicias, servis, fit, non oboedio, stabit omnipotentis); 'recciderunt' read as 'conciderunt' (fallen); 'coamentem' taken as 'fellow-madman'; stray 'I' before 'uiuis' and the word 'uiuis' are unclear and left untranslated. Line 1: Lucifer's text of Acts 13:8 names the magician Etoemus (Greek Hetoimas, 'ready'), where the Vulgate has Elymas.

Several evident scanning errors read as intended: 'in Hebrum' as 'in Hebraeos', 'sumas' as 'sumus', 'indicio dei' as 'iudicio dei', 'haeretico Amano' as 'haeretico Arriano', 'atcoovacovxai' as Greek 'homoousion', 'pronuntiantis' as 'pronuntiatis'. 'uoluntatis illius sagenae' ('the net of his will') is odd and may be corrupt. The Deuteronomy quotation 'peccauerunt non ei filii maculati' is rendered literally; its sense is obscure in the Latin.

25.1: 'cur non esse Arrianus noluerit' is a double negative as printed; translated by the evident sense 'refused to be an Arian'. The clause 'quia pati non facere dignum sit iniuriam Christianos, interfici' is awkward and may be corrupt; translated as it stands. 26.1: 'ludas' read as 'Iudas' throughout (scanning error). 27.1: 'ducis' read as 'dicis'; 'operarios' as 'operarius'; 'nidemus' as 'uidemus'; 'r.ed(i £ )um' as 'reditum' (profit); 'mdentes' as 'uidentes'; 'Romam' as 'Romani'. 'crede in deum Iesum' is translated as given ('in God Jesus'); other witnesses of Acts 16:31 read 'dominum' (Lord).

Many evident scanning errors corrected silently: 'dealitas' read as deitas (Godhead); 'rdiqua pedibus sunt' as reliqua pedibus suis; 'begtia', 'eomu', 'faeie', 'indicium' (iudicium), 'sentiebant' (seruiebant), 'nisus' (uisus), 'eiup' (eius), 'ininriosos'; stray marks 'I', 'j', 'N', 'P', '}' omitted. In 30.1 'imperium eiregnum corrumpetur' is garbled; translated as 'imperium eius [et] regnum non corrumpetur', following the sense of Dan. 7:14. 'anticipauit' (twice, in the Old Latin Daniel) rendered 'came forward' and 'arrived'. In 28.1 'quod uerus sit filius' appears to need a negative to fit the Arian position described; rendered with a bracketed [denied].

31: ‘dei sernos’ read as ‘dei seruos’; ‘Arrus’ as ‘Arrius’. 32: ‘de collectis tuis’ taken as ‘your associates’ (perhaps for ‘collegis’). ‘secundum sacerdotibus praecepta’ seems corrupt (perhaps ‘secundum apostoli praecepta’); rendered literally. 33: ‘honeste’ where the biblical text has ‘abunde’ (richly); rendered as given. ‘tecum spuniamus’ is corrupt; read as ‘puniamus’ (punish). ‘Christianos-. stianos’ is a dittography for ‘Christianos’. The final sentence is somewhat obscure.

Several scanning errors read as evident: 'stultam' as stultum, 'obsedit ore' as obsedit me (Ps 21:17), 'patricii' as patrii, 'Margariein' as Garizin (cf. 2 Macc 6:2), 'misereri' as sacrificare/immolare is uncertain (rendered 'make them sacrifice', following 2 Macc 6:8). 'sufflammati sunt' taken as 'were burned' (2 Macc 6:11 combusti sunt); 'speculas' taken as 'caves' (speluncas). 'aduenit ergo uidere' read as 'one could see'. In 34.1 '<si>' is an editorial supplement; the sentence 'mentiri te cognoscere ... poteris' is awkward and rendered by sense. In 35.1 'existimant' (plural) is odd for Antiochus; probably existimauit.

nodes.text: IV. ON NOT SPARING THOSE WHO OFFEND AGAINST GOD.

When you saw, emperor, that you had been overcome on every side by the servants of God, you said that you had suffered and were suffering insult from us, contrary to the warnings of the sacred scriptures; you say that we have been insolent towards you, whom it was fitting to honour. If any of the worshippers of God has ever spared apostates, let what you say of us be true. Where shall we begin, so that we may prove that, just as you are now rebuked by us, so all who strayed have been rebuked by the worshippers of God? Where, if not from the deeds of Moses, the servant of God? We read in Exodus that Moses went up the mountain, after the covenant had been handed to him, and killed very many of them on account of the guilt of idolatry. Moses stood, it says, at the gates of the camp and said: 'Who is ready for the Lord? Let him come to me.' And all the sons of Levi gathered to him, and he said to them: 'Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Each of you put his sword on his thigh, and go through and return from gate to gate through the camp, and each of you kill his brother, and each his kinsman, and each his neighbour.' And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them. And there fell of the people on that day about three thousand men. And Moses said to them: 'You have filled your hands today for the Lord, each against son or brother, so that a blessing may be given among you.' We are insulting to you as Moses was to that foolish people; nor were the things said or done by Moses pleasing to them, since they had already chosen not to serve God, who had rescued them from the power of Pharaoh, but that calf which the fire had cast for them. So you too, now bound over not to God but to the idolatry of Arius, take it ill that you are shown to have erred, you keep crying that we are defiant, you say that we have committed an outrageous crime against you, in that we dared to say to the emperor of the Roman realm: 'You do wrong, Constantius, to bring idolatry into the Church.' Moses, the first of the prophets, that man most beloved of God, pursued with the sword those whose imitator you have made yourself, and am I branded by you as defiant because I said that God has abandoned you and that you have bound yourself over to idolatry? Further, sacred scripture proclaims that the sons of Israel committed fornication with the daughters of the Moabites, and that, invited by them, they ate things sacrificed to idols and worshipped those same idols; and because Phinehas the priest, kindled with the zeal of devotion, blazed up so against them, and above all because he slew the idolaters with the sword in the midst of the assembly, he so pleased God that it is written that at this deed the wrath of the angry Lord was stilled, and that he himself was made exceedingly eminent before the Lord: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has restrained my wrath from the sons of Israel, in that he was zealous with zeal among them, and I did not consume the sons of Israel in my zeal. And behold, I will give him my covenant, a covenant of peace, to him and to his seed with him, as a covenant of eternal priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.' And do you think us defiant because we tell the truth to you while you err? Do you suppose that when we displease you we are not then pleasing God? But I beg you to say, Constantius, by what authority you would have us desert the way of the righteous patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs, and take up this new way of yours which the devil had established through Arius. Were you warned in a dream, and was it said to you that you should not allow us to hold the way of Christ which Abel, Enoch, Noah, Melchizedek, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Joshua son of Nun, Job, the judges and the other kings held, that is David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Josiah, which all the prophets, apostles and martyrs had held, which all had held who are found to have pleased God?

If this was said to you by the prince of demons, hear what God has decreed should be done concerning you, through the glorious prophet Moses: 'But if a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives a sign or a portent, and comes performing signs or portents and speaks to you, saying: Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know, you shall not hear the word of that prophet or dreamer, for the Lord God is testing you, to see whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul. You shall go after the Lord your God and fear him, and you shall keep his commandments and hear his voice, and you shall cleave to him. And that prophet or dreamer of dreams, let them die; for they have spoken to lead you astray from the Lord your God.' Do you recognise what you are ordered to suffer? For whether you say you were warned in a dream or wish to set yourself up before us as a prophet, you are an enemy of God, since you want us to abandon the apostolic faith and take up that which denies the only Son of God. For it is clear that all those whom I have listed became so great and such men because they believed in the only Son of God, since he who does not believe in the Son does not have the Father either, but he who believes in the Son has both the Father and the Son. Since this is the voice of blessed John, and since the choir of the holy apostles is in accord with him, you surely ought to understand that, just as the apostles believed, so the patriarchs and prophets had believed before, and so all who are known to have been honoured for the merit of faith. For you will not be able to prove to me that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob believed one way and John and all his fellow apostles another. For if the apostles did not believe as the patriarchs believed, why does blessed Paul call all to take hold of the faith of Abraham? But you say: 'I am charging you with being insolent, with having been insulting to the emperor, and you rehearse the cause of the faith.' Of the faith, certainly, so that I may prove you sacrilegious, so that I may prove that you have strayed from the way of truth; this is why I seem insulting to you, because I tell you that you have deserted the path of all the worshippers of God and taken up that which those have held and still hold who served and still serve not God but a phantasm. So concerning you, who urge me to withdraw from God, hear what God has ordained through Moses should be done: 'But if your brother by father or mother, or your son or your daughter, or the woman who is in your bosom, or the friend who is equal to your own soul, entreats you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know, nor your fathers, from the gods of the nations which are around you, near or far, do not consent to go with him and do not listen to him; your eye shall not spare him, nor shall you greet him, nor shall you hide him. You shall surely denounce him. Your hands shall be upon him first to kill him, and the hands of your people last. And you shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to draw [you] away from the Lord your God.' Not knowing, indeed, that you, who invite me to abandon God, are commanded to be killed, you say: 'Lucifer insults me.' Or will you deny that you invited us to take up idolatry? If you think it should be denied, the statements of the bishops of your sect, that is, of your fellow blasphemers, will convict you; the documents will convict you which were read out by you and given at Rome to bishops, even catholic ones, for this purpose, namely that your blasphemy might be strengthened in every place.

Do you not feel what darkness of errors you have fallen into? Do you not see how you may perish? When you see why Achar, one of the people, acted against the divine warnings, why he stole from Jericho a certain portion of clothing, silver and gold, [and] that he was punished with death for it, consider what will happen to you, who deny the eternal divine majesty of the only Son of God. Hear what was done concerning Achar, and at last look to your salvation, return to the Church of God, from which that renegade serpent who also overthrew Adam and Eve has driven you away through the Arians: 'And the Lord,' it says, 'was with Joshua, and his name was over all the earth. And the sons of Israel were grievously negligent and committed fraud concerning the devoted thing. And the Lord was angered with wrath against the sons of Israel. And Joshua sent men to Ai, which is next to Bethel, saying: Spy out Ai. And the men went up and spied out Ai. And they returned to Joshua and said to him: Let not all the people go up, but let two or three thousand men go up and lay waste the city. Do not lead the whole people there, for they are few. And there went up with him about three thousand men, and they fled before the men who were in Ai. And the men of Ai killed thirty-six men of them, and pursued them from the gate and crushed them on the slope, and the heart of the people was terrified and became like water. And Joshua tore his garments, and Joshua fell on his face before God until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads, and Joshua said: I pray you, Lord, why did your servant bring this people across the Jordan, to deliver it to the Amorite, to destroy us? If we had stayed in the land, we would have dwelt by the Jordan. And what shall I say, since Israel has turned its back before its enemy? And the Canaanite will hear, and all who dwell in the land, and they will surround us and crush us from the land. And what will you do for your great name? And the Lord said to Joshua: Get up; why have you fallen on your face? The people has sinned and transgressed my covenant which I made with them, and they have stolen from the devoted thing and put it among their goods. The sons of Israel will not be able to stand before the face of their enemies; they will turn their backs in the sight of their enemies, because they have become accursed. I will not be with you any longer unless you remove the devoted thing from among yourselves. Get up, sanctify the people and say: Let it be sanctified for tomorrow. For thus says the Lord God of Israel: There is a devoted thing among you; you will not be able to stand against your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among you. And assemble in the morning, all of you, by tribes, and the tribe which is shown by God in the morning, bring it forward by clans; the clan which the Lord shows, bring forward man by man, and whoever is shown by the Lord shall be burned with fire, and all that is his, because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord and done iniquity in Israel. And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought the people forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was shown. And they were brought forward by clans, and the clan of Zerah was shown. And he brought forward the clan of Zerah by households, and the household of Zabdi was shown. And the household was brought forward man by man, and Achar son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, was shown. And Joshua said to Achar: Give honour today to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession, and tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me. And Achar answered Joshua and said: Truly I have sinned before the Lord God of Israel; thus and thus I did. I saw among the spoil a fine embroidered garment and two hundred didrachms of silver and one bar of gold of fifty didrachms, and I coveted it and took it, and behold, these things are hidden in my tent, and the silver is hidden beneath them. And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and these things were hidden in the tent and the silver beneath them. And they took them from the tent and brought them to Joshua and to the elders of Israel and laid them before God. And they seized Achar son of Carmi and led into the valley of Achar him and his sons and daughters and his calves and his beasts of burden and his sheep and his tent and all that was his. And all Israel was with him, and they led them to Emek Achor. And Joshua said to Achar: Why have you destroyed us? May the Lord destroy you, as on this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and they heaped over him a great pile of stones. And the Lord ceased from the indignation of his wrath.' Consider, Constantius, after what pattern you are to perish, unless you look to yourself, what punishments you are to pay for eternity. Achar met such an end on account of transgressing the commandments; what you deserve may be understood from this, that you are an apostate. For if he, because he had some of the devoted thing, was punished with such destruction, how much more you! Without doubt you will be punished more heavily, you who have become accursed by denying the Son of God.

In this we are wicked in your eyes, in this proud and stubborn, in this insolent: that we say to you, 'You have committed sacrilege by being a denier of the only Son of God'; that we say, 'Look to yourself, snatch your soul from the snares of the devil.' What new thing are we bishops doing if we say to you the things you deserve to hear? For we find that most holy Samuel, priest of God, said to King Saul these things, which you will read below: 'Pains and groans will be brought upon you. Because you have held the word of the Lord of no account, the Lord will hold you of no account, so that you may not reign'; and again: 'Since you have held the word of the Lord of no account, God will also bring you to nothing, so that you may not be king over Israel'; and below: 'The Lord will tear the kingdom from Israel out of your hand today, and will give it to your neighbour, who is better than you.' If he said these things to Saul because he had passed over the commands of the Lord, why do you think we ought not to have said with a free voice that you are sacrilegious, and that unless you turn yourself to God, he will bring you to nothing? If we had not exhorted you, if we were not calling you to make amends, you would rightly say that you are hated by us. Rather, when you hear us say, 'Repent, emperor, correct your ways, so that you may find room for mercy,' I think you ought to have considered that you are indeed cherished by us, loved by us; and you curse us for this, that we remain in the apostolic faith; you return evil for good. We do not wonder if you, from the time you withdraw from the will of God and do not cease doing the desire of the devil, return evils to those who ask God that good be done to you and who desire it, since acting wickedly is ingrained in you, inasmuch as you have made the passage from good to evil, that is, to the devil. If you persecute us who love you and desire that all the highest things come to you, it is nothing great or new, since Saul too persecuted this Samuel, prophet and priest of the Lord. He persecuted the man by whom he had been anointed king, and whose prayers were directed to the Lord in constant supplication for the safety of this very persecutor. If you do not believe us that we priests of God grieve for you, because you have drunk in such darkness of errors, because you are thus slaughtering yourself, believe God saying to Samuel concerning Saul: 'How long will you mourn for Saul? Behold, I am driving him out, so that he may not reign over Israel'; and above: 'And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: I repent that I appointed Saul king, since he has turned away from me and has not upheld my words. And Samuel was grieved and cried to the Lord all night and before dawn.' Although Samuel the priest did these things for the safety of King Saul, yet Saul afterwards persecuted Samuel, not knowing, wretch, that he was persecuting a prophet and priest of the Lord; so you too, not knowing what you are doing, persecute us, who desire you to please God, and you love those who drag you with them to eternal death, to the everlasting displeasure of the Lord; you are indignant that you hear the truth, though you see that Samuel, the priest of the Lord, did not flatter the king. Or was it fitting for our predecessors to do one thing, and for us another? Because we tell you the truth, we seem proud to you. What have you heard from us? Surely that you are a murderer. If we lie, then we are rightly called insolent, then rightly proud, by you; but if we speak the truth, we are not insolent, but men who imitate those who, by not flattering those entrusted to them but warning them beforehand for their salvation, deserved to be made most beloved to God. When the king of Israel sent to kill the prophet Elisha — if you had not read that Elisha said to those who were with him, 'Have you seen that the son of that murderer has sent to take off my head?', you might rightly prosecute me as guilty of insults. The prophet, full of the Holy Spirit, called the king of Israel the son of a murderer, that is, the son of the devil, not because he called his fleshly father a murderer, but the devil, whose son he too showed himself to be, as you now reveal yourself by your deeds, by persecuting the servants of God and daring to kill the prophets of that Clemency. The devil incites your hearts to do all these things. That this is so, hear the Lord saying to the Jews in the gospel: 'You are born of the devil as your father, and you wish to do the desires of your father; for he was a murderer from the beginning.' The prophet of the Lord, I say, full of the Holy Spirit, calls the king of Israel the son of a murderer, that is, of the devil; and do you think we insult you because we say that you are the killer of the servants of God, the butcher of our bodies, a man whose every thought is injustice, a destroyer of religion, a denier of the only Son of God? What we see you do, this we say of you; what you are, this we proclaim you to be. You call us insolent because we tell you what you are.

Tell me, I would like to know, why the king of Israel deserved to hear such things from the Lord: 'Because you have done good before me and have done according to my heart, and according to my soul to the house of Ahab, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit for you on the throne of Israel'? Tell me, I say, why he deserved to hear these things from God? Because he spared the enemies of God? Or because he pursued them most fiercely, even with the sword, or because he killed the idolatrous son of Ahab and his forty sons, because he threw Queen Jezebel, once killed, to the dogs, and destroyed all the servants of Baal with all the priests and prophets of confusion by the edge of the sword, because he destroyed the images — [is that why] he pleases God? What ought we to have done regarding you, so that you might not brand us guilty of insult toward you, whom we see holding the ways of Ahab and Jezebel? What you do is not new: to act against God, to attack his house, to persecute his bishops, those through whom he warns you to look to yourself, so that, while there is room for repentance, you may drag yourself away from evil. Before you there were men like you in sacrilege, serving idols in the same way, having abandoned the God of their fathers. In the second book of Chronicles we hear that Amaziah, king of Judah, was warned by God through a prophet that none of the sons of Israel whom he had hired for a hundred thousand talents of silver should set out with him to war, namely because God had abandoned Israel, since they had abandoned God and served idols. The king obeyed the prophet's words; he believed it was God's threat. Why does he do these things? After he subdues his adversaries, he thought their idols should be taken and carried over to his kingdom and should themselves be worshipped; and because that man of God told him he had not acted well in abandoning God to worship the idols of the nations, this king vigorously persecuted the prophet of the Lord. You see that in you who have turned to apostasy there has always been one single mind to persecute those who wish you well. 'And it came to pass,' says holy scripture, 'after Amaziah came to strike Idumaea, he also brought from there the gods of Mount Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and worshipped before them, and himself sacrificed to them. And the wrath of the Lord came upon him, upon Amaziah, and he sent to him the prophet Baneas, and Baneas said to him: Why have you sought the gods of a people, who did not deliver their own people from your hand? And it came to pass, as he was speaking to him, that he said to him: Have I made you the king's counsellor? Beware lest you be scourged.' You see, Constantius, how senseless you are made, after it has pleased you to live serving the devil, after it has pleased you not to know God almighty, after you have chosen that you must set up idolatry as an insult to God. For as he said, 'Have I made you the king's counsellor? Beware lest you be scourged,' so you too say: 'Did I choose you as my counsellors, so that I should not act as pleases me, so that I should not hold this way which Arius held?' And do you not see after what pattern Arius perished? How vengeance was taken on him by God? Meanwhile, since you say that we are insulting to you, see that this man of God did not spare that king, your fellow in sacrilege, but after he was told, 'Be silent, lest you be scourged,' said to him: 'I know that the Lord will destroy you, who have done this and have not listened to my counsel.' In what do you find us insulting? Surely because we say to you: we know that, unless you take care to turn to God, the Lord will condemn you to eternal punishment. This is the insult, this the whole injury: that you are told by the bishops of God that you will perish forever unless you correct your ways. That king did not believe the man of God. What at once befell him holy scripture tells thus: 'And at the time when Amaziah departed from the Lord, they rose up against him [...]. And he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish, and they killed him [...] on horses.' So too the deeds of your wicked men will be able to preserve, guard and defend you, just as they did him who said to the man of God speaking for his safety: 'Have I appointed you counsellor to the king? Be silent, lest you be scourged.' It is not we who first do this, if we say to you, who are erring, resisting the ordinance of God, labouring to establish new ways: you do wrong not to go by the way by which all worshippers of God have reached the heavenly kingdoms.

You have read that King Uzziah was rebuked by the priests of the Lord for having dared to do unlawful things: 'And he entered,' says scripture, 'into the temple of the Lord to place incense upon the altar. And after him entered Azariah the priest, and with him thirty priests of the Lord, sons of valour, and they rose up against King Uzziah and said to him: It is not lawful for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been sanctified to burn incense. Go out from the holy place, for you have departed from the Lord, and this will not be to your honour from the Lord God.' Do you say that the priests of the Lord were insulting to that king, or not? If they were not insulting, then neither should we seem so to you, since you hear from us things like those he heard: it is not lawful for you, Constantius, an Arian, to assemble with the people of God; it is not lawful for you, the author of the idolatry of the Arian heresy, a denier of the only Son of God, to judge concerning the priests of God, a sacrilegious man pretending to be a Christian, when you are the forerunner of Antichrist. It will not be good for you that, removing the priests of God, you ordain his adversaries, that is, the colleagues of your sacrilege. When you hear these things, you are angry with us; King Uzziah too was angry then with those priests of the Lord. But note that they, dedicated to God, kept the honour of their station forever, while Uzziah was at once spotted with the mottling of leprosy, to his everlasting disgrace. 'And Uzziah was angry,' it says, 'and in his hand was the altar [censer], to burn incense on his altar. And leprosy appeared on his forehead in the sight of the priests in the house of the Lord.' These things are so, and do you think that you, a stubborn transgressor, do not incur offence with him who has commanded us to perform for his glory the offices of the priesthood forever? What is this pride of ours, Constantius, or what arrogance? Unless it is that we see you are diseased, pestilent, being indeed an Arian; that we observe in you that elephantiasis which Arius had; that we urge you to withdraw from the people of God, just as those priests of the Lord compelled Uzziah to go out of the temple; that we thus press you to give honour to God. For if the priests of God drove Uzziah from the court of God because they remembered that by divine command lepers were forbidden to enter the temple before purification, how much more, consider, are we right to drive you out of the church of Christ, from the house of the Lord, since it is not lawful for a heretic to assemble with catholics, the insane with the sane, one full of unclean spirits with those in whom the Spirit of God dwells. What insult is this, if we priests of the Lord, fired with that zeal with which our predecessors always were, tell you what serves our salvation and yours? 'Lucifer is insolent,' you say. Insolent in this, that I press you to cast off the elephantiasis of Arius, and that, through this faith which the most blessed apostles preached and which, as you see, we hold, you may gain soundness for your mind and, wholly snatched from the snares of the devil, rejoice forever that you have been sought out by God. You who accuse us of enormous haughtiness, have you found written what Josiah king of Judah did to your fellow-sacrilegists, to such as you are seen to be today, how he pursued very many of them even after death, consuming their bones with fire? But it was fitting for that king to pursue the enemies of God with such zeal; for us bishops, us priests of God, it was unworthy to resist you when you bring idolatry into the church? He killed your fellow-sacrilegists with the sword, and pursued even remains long buried, desiring to be found a most faithful worshipper of God; we, on the contrary, ought not to resist you even with a word, you, the friend of the enemy of God, you, dearest of all to the angels turned to apostasy, you, who through this blasphemy of yours have become an enemy to God?

Hear, then, in the fourth book of Kingdoms what Josiah, servant of the Lord, king of Judah, obtained on account of what he did concerning your fellow-unclean ones, and at last stop saying of us: 'They are proud and insulting.' 'He did,' it says, 'what is right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father David, and did not turn aside to the right or the left.' Likewise below, after he had rebuilt the house of the Lord and the priest had sent the book of the law to the king: 'And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his garments. And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Achbor son of Micaiah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the king's servant, saying: Inquire of the Lord for me and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found, for the great wrath of the Lord has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not hear the words of this book, to do according to all that is written. And Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam and Shaphan and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe, and she lived in Jerusalem. And they spoke to her accordingly. And she said to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring evils upon this place and upon those who dwell in it, according to all the words of this book which the king of Judah has read, because they have forsaken me and turned to foreign gods and provoked me by the works of their hands. And my wrath has been kindled against this place and will not be quenched. And to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the Lord, you shall say this: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: As for my words which you have heard, and you revered [them] before my face, because you heard what I spoke against this place and its inhabitants, that it should become a desert and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before me, I too have heard, says the Lord of hosts. Therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be added [to them] in peace, and your eyes will not see all the evils which I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants. And they brought back word to the king. And King Josiah sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah in Jerusalem. And the king went up to the Lord, and all the men of Judah and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from the least to the greatest. And the king read in the hearing of the people all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord. And the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord before the Lord, to walk after the Lord and keep his commandments and testimonies and precepts with all his heart and all his soul, to establish all the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people entered into the covenant which the king made from the book. And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and those who kept the ephod to cast out of the house of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and Asherah and all the host of heaven. And he burned them outside Jerusalem in the burning-place of the brook Kidron, and took their ashes and scattered them in the brook, and went to Bethel. And he burned the priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places of the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem; they burned incense to Baal and to the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven. And they carried [the Asherah] out of the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem to the brook Kidron, and he ground it to ash and threw it on the tomb of the sons of the common people. And he pulled down the houses of those who were in the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings. And he brought in all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the holy places where the priests burned incense, from Geba as far as Beersheba, and he pulled down their high places.' And below: 'And he defiled Topheth, which was in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so that no one should make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Moloch. [And he took away the horses which] the kings of Judah had set up to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, by the [chamber] of the eunuch, which was in the precincts, and he burned the chariot of the sun with fire in the house which the kings of Israel built, on that high place, to Baal and all the host of heaven. And the altars that were on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king pulled down and removed from there, and threw their ashes into the brook Kidron. And the high places which they had made before Jerusalem, which were on the right of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon the king built to Astarte, the image of the Sidonians, and to Chemosh the idol, and to Milcom the image of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled. And he broke the pillars in pieces and filled their places with human bones. And the altar which was in Bethel, the high place which Jeroboam son of Nebat made, by which he made Israel sin, that altar and high place he pulled down and broke its stones and ground them to dust, and burned their groves. And King Josiah turned and saw the tombs that were there on the mountain, and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it, according to the word which the man of God spoke when Jeroboam stood at the altar on the feast day.' What do you learn, Constantius, was done by a king who worshipped God? And because we strike you with a word as you bring idolatry into the church, do you say, 'Lucifer insults me'? Whereas, had you been a man of that time, you could have been destroyed by the sword, or had you already died, even your bones, being sacrilegious, would have been brought to nothing by fire. He strikes with the sword those guilty of so great a crime, and was it not fitting for us to wound you even with a word? You see meanwhile in this place also that those kings, your fellow-sacrilegists, brought into the city of God, into the house of the Lord and into his temple, the idolatry which this Josiah, the king most devoted to God, exterminated; and do not think that you alone have undertaken to carry out this work against God. So I do not want you to say: 'If I were acting wickedly, God would already have taken vengeance on me'; but rather I beg you to see that you are held captive by the devil, that you live in his power, just as did those kings whose work King Josiah pursued.

Because we curse your blasphemies, because we resist your wicked conspiracies, we seem to you to be insulting. So too, to the Jews, whose imitator you are, the most holy prophets and the most blessed apostles seemed insolent and proud. In the book of the prophet Amos, 'And Amaziah, the priest in Bethel, sent,' it says, 'to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos is making a conspiracy against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land will not be able to bear his words, because Amos says this: Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will be led captive from its land. And Amaziah said to Amos: Go, depart into the land of Judah, and stay there, and there you shall prophesy. But in Bethel you shall no longer prophesy, because it is the king's sanctuary and will be the house of the kingdom. And Amos answered and said to Amaziah: I was not a prophet, nor am I the son of a prophet, but I was a goatherd, plucking [figs], and the Lord took me from the sheep and said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel. And now hear the word of the Lord: You say, You shall not prophesy in Israel, and there shall be no gathering in the house of Jacob. Because of this the Lord God says this: Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, your land shall be measured with a line, and you shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall be led captive from its land.' When you see that these things were done by him who had willed that truth and reproof be announced to his erring people, why should you call us insolent, why insulting, because we tell you, who are astray, what is true, because we do not listen to your voice saying: 'Do not believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed, but believe as Arius has handed down'? In what things are we found proud in your eyes? Only in this, that we curse your sacrileges and avoid your commands like swords and poisons. This was not first done by us; all those who have already pleased God, holding this faith which we preach, did this; none of his servants was afraid to undergo death for God, none of his servants considered the kinds of tortures which are inflicted by you tyrants, but he kept his commands before his eyes. So Tobit is found to have become glorious and outstanding before the Lord, while he fears not the edict of your fellow-reprobate king, but only the almighty God. Believe that this is so from Tobit himself, who says: 'When King Sennacherib came fleeing from Judaea because of the defence which the Lord made against them, because of his blasphemies which he blasphemed, he killed in his anger many of the sons of Israel; but I wrapped their bodies and buried them. And it was reported to the king that I was burying [them], and he sought to kill me. But I fled, and all my property was plundered, and nothing was left to me but my wife Anna and Tobias my son. And it happened after forty-five days that his sons killed that king, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place there. And when I had come into my house and my wife Anna and my son Tobias had been restored to me, at Pentecost, our feast day, which is the holy [feast] of weeks, a good dinner was made for me, and I reclined to dine, and a table was set for me, and I saw a great many dishes, and I said to Tobias my son: Go and bring whatever poor man you find of our brothers who are captives in Nineveh, who yet keep God in mind with their whole heart; bring him, and let him eat this dinner together with me; see, I am waiting for you, son, until you come. And Tobias went out to look for some poor captive of our brothers, and returned and said to me: Father. And I said: What is it, son? And he said to me: See, one of our nation has been killed, with a noose put round him, and thrown out. And I went out, leaving my dinner before I had tasted anything of it, and I take him up from the street [and put him] in a place by me until the sun should set, so that I might bury him. And having returned, I washed and ate my dinner with grief, and I remembered the word of the prophet Amos which he spoke in Bethel, saying: Your feast days shall be turned into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; and I wept. And after the sun had set, I went and dug and buried him. And all my neighbours mocked me, saying: How is it that this man is not afraid? For he has already been sought out to be killed on account of this matter, and he fled, and again he has begun to bury the dead.'

Since, therefore, you see that the servants of God have never feared your cruelty, the cruelty of tyrants, and cannot fear it now, but have kept and keep in mind the commands of the Lord, how do you see fit to judge us insolent? Plainly because, with God acting, we trample your power like mud. Our own strength does not do this; rather the mercy of him whom you see fit to curse in us grants it. God says to the prophet Ezekiel: 'Son of man, I am sending you to the house of Israel, because they and their fathers have embittered me up to this very day. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord, whether they hear or tremble, for it is an embittering house; and they shall know that you are a prophet in their midst. And you, son of man, do not fear them nor tremble before their face, for they will rage and rush upon you all around, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions; do not fear their words and do not tremble before their face, for it is an embittering house. And you shall speak my words to them, if perhaps they will hear or be afraid, for it is an embittering house.' We seem defiant to you, as this prophet, devoted to God alone, seemed to those whose darkness you follow; plainly it was for this that the prophet Ezekiel seemed defiant among the Jews, your fellow-apostates, for this that he seemed proud to the kings of Israel: because he fulfilled the commands of the Lord, because he spoke to them what God had commanded him to speak. Rightly do you call us proud, us through whom he willed all his commands to be brought to the knowledge of the believing peoples. Rightly, I say, do you mark us bishops of God as insolent, if we say to you the things which God willed to be said to you. You hate those who love you, you persecute those who wish you well, but we cannot fear the gnashings of your butchery. For you hear the Lord say: 'And you, son of man, do not fear them nor tremble before their face, for they will rage and rush upon you all around, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions. Do not fear their words, do not tremble before their face, for it is an embittering house.' We cannot, I say, fear the threats of your rule, because your scorpion-like strength is nothing against us, whom you perceive to be covered by the power of God, whose defender and protector you observe God to be. So we shall not cease pressing the Lord's commands upon you, keeping our fears for him alone, who says: 'Son of man, go in to the house of Israel and speak my words to them, for you are not sent to a people of deep speech, to Israel, nor to many peoples of another voice or another tongue, nor heavy of tongue, whose speech you will not understand. And if I had sent you to such, they perhaps would have heard your words; but the house of Israel will not be willing to hear you, because they are not willing to hear me, for the whole house of Israel is contentious and hard of heart. And see, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your steadfastness against their contention, and you will always be firmer than rock. Do not fear them nor be afraid before their face, for it is an embittering house.' Which of us will be able to fear you, whom you see made solid and firm by the power of God to beat back your defiance, standing immovable with fixed step against your rage, as rocks strong in their mass are wont [to stand] against the swelling sea? This is why you judge us your enemies, because we urge you to become, from a scorpion, a servant of God. For now you will not be able to doubt that you are one of the scorpions, of those of whom you have heard it said by the Lord to the prophet: 'And you, son of man, do not fear nor tremble before their face, for they will rage and rush upon you all around, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions.' This is why we are insulting to you, because you see yourself called a scorpion by us. If God had not said that you are a scorpion, you would rightly call me insulting; but now you show by your deeds that you are a scorpion, and you cry out in vain that you suffer insult from us. God says that you are a scorpion, and are you angry with me for calling you by that name? What insult is this, if it is said to you: unless you turn to God, you will always be, as you are now, one of the scorpions, one of the most savage enemies of God?

Run through the rest of the prophet Ezekiel, and dare to call me insolent, proud, insulting, obstinate: 'And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, see, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel, and you will hear a word from my mouth and you will threaten them from me in that which I say to the wicked man: You shall surely die. And you did not warn him nor speak, so as to warn the wicked man to turn from his ways that he might live; that wicked man shall die in his injustice, and I will require his blood from your hand. And you, if you warn the wicked man and he does not turn away from his wickedness and his way, that wicked man shall die in his injustice, and you will free your soul. And in that in which a just man turns away from his just deeds and commits a sin, and I put torment before his face, he shall die, because you did not warn him. And he shall die in his sins, because his just deeds will not be remembered, and I will require his blood from your hand. But you, if you warn the just man not to sin, and he does not sin, that just man shall surely live, because you warned him, and you will save your soul.' What do you say to this, Constantius? Will the priests of God have to keep silent and hide his divine commands, or is it right to lay open to you all the precepts of the Lord? Shall we bring the whole will of God to those entrusted to us, or shall we cheat ourselves of it, to our own slaughter? For the Lord says that he will require your blood from me; but rather, if you do not obey God, whose divine warnings we press upon you, you will die a wicked man in your own wickedness, and the salvation of your soul will no longer be required of us, since we were not frightened by your threats, but feared only him who has commanded that no one besides himself is to be feared, since we confronted you in the name of the Lord God so that you might rescue yourself from your abominable paths. So as not to seem to do insult to you, the emperor, what ought I to have done at the time when I declare you were born to turn us, the servants of God, from the way of truth? When Nebuchadnezzar had sent Holofernes, the commander of his army, and he was besieging Jerusalem, what does Judith pray to God? Surely, that he would destroy the enemies of Israel. Did she not say: 'Guard against those who rise up against your house'? 'O Lord God of my father Simeon, who gave a sword for vengeance on the foreigners who violated the womb of a virgin to defilement, and uncovered the thigh to [her] ruin, and defiled the womb to disgrace. For you said: It shall not be so; and you did it. Therefore you gave their rulers to slaughter, and their bed, which had received the beloved, to blood, and you struck down servants together with the mighty, upon their thrones. And you gave their women as plunder and their daughters into captivity and all the plunder to be divided among your beloved sons, who were zealous with your zeal and abhorred the defilement of your race and called upon you for your help. My God, you will hear me, a widow. For you did the things before them, and those things, and those after, and now, and those that are to come. For all your ways are prepared, your creation in providence. For see, the Assyrians are filled with their might and exalted in horse and rider, and they glory in the arm of their foot soldiers; they have trusted in shields and the drawn bow and slings, and they have not known that you are the Lord who crushes wars. The Lord is your name. Cast down their strength, Eternal One, crush their multitude by your power, and bring down their stubbornness in your wrath. For they have planned to frustrate your holy things, to defile the tabernacle of rest of your honourable name, to seize with iron the horn of your altar. Look upon their pride, give into my hand, a widow's, the strength which I have planned, and strike down by the lips of my persuasion the ruler with the [servant] and the ruler with his servant; shatter his substance by the hand of a widow. For your might is not in numbers, nor your power and your gift in the strong; but you are the God of the humble, the help of the weak, the upholder of the feeble, the saviour of the despairing. Yes, God of my father and God of the inheritance of Israel, Lord, ruler of heaven and earth, creator of the waters, king of all creation, hear my supplication; give cunning and persuasion for the wound and bruise of those who have planned harsh things against your covenant and your holy house and the heights of Zion and the house held by your sons. Bring it about over every nation and every tribe, that they may know that you are the God of all power and might, and there is no other defender of the race of Israel besides you.'

What will your prudent mind deign to think of this? Will you be able to say, after this supplication poured out to God against the enemies of religion, that we strive against you wrongly because we say to you: either correct your crooked ways and do not please yourself in the power of your rule, or know that you will come to nothing? What else are we, the servants of God, the priests of his divine majesty, doing today, but what was done by those whose imitators we long to be found? For I think it right not to abandon the peoples entrusted to us in this great persecution brought upon us by you, but to exhort them [that] he whose we are is powerful to rescue us from the hands of his enemies; that you, the enemy of the house of God, are not to be feared; that they must recognise that you are nothing, since evidently our God and Lord, who is almighty, will bring to nothing all your impious attempts set up against his house. What injury is done to you here by us? What insult is heaped on the Roman emperor by the bishops of the living God, if you are asked to have eternal life, or if it is said to you that, because you have taken up arms against the house of God, unless you correct yourself you will perish in great ruin? For why do we set before you the destruction of all the enemies of God's house? Only so that either, terrified by the fear of God, you may change yourself, or, when you have caused yourself to be punished for ever, we may triumph secure on every side, because your blood cannot be required of us by God, and because we shall have seen the destruction of the adversaries of his Church. Persevere, then, in this injustice of yours, and you will find what follows upon you for such great deserts. 'Lucifer is puffed up with pride,' you say, because he tells you the truth. What would you have had me do at this time, when you, the forerunner of Antichrist, raised arms against the house of God to kill us? At the time when you stood forth as the denier of the only Son of God? Should I have kept silent and let you, a wolf, come to lay waste the flock of God? Or do you judge it would have been right for us shepherds to go to meet you, ready with dry throat to devour us and those entrusted to us? It was a great enough wonder that this woman Judith, longing to please God, killed the enemy with her own hand; and should we, appointed shepherds by the Lord, not have resisted you even with a word? The Lord says in the Gospel: 'The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep; he who is a hireling and not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf seizes them and scatters them, because he is a hireling and has no care for the sheep.' What then were we to do, so as not to seem to have been insulting to you? We recognised you as a wolf, we saw that you had stretched out your hands against the sheep of the Lord, we observed you trying at one time to tear apart all who call on the name of the Lord. Would it have been right for us to show ourselves not shepherds but hirelings? He says to blessed Peter: 'Feed my lambs,' and again: 'Feed my little sheep'; and do you, coming as a wolf, want those who are found to be successors of blessed Peter to play the part of hirelings? Those whom he had long ago promised to his people through Jeremiah, saying: 'And I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they will feed you, feeding with discipline'; and he did not say: 'I will give you the emperor Constantius, who can turn you into the devil's prey.' You may say that we act wrongly because we resist your sacrilege, protected by the power of God.

Let us see also what was done, at the time when your fellow-tyrant Antiochus stood forth as persecutor of our religion, by those who remembered that no one besides God is to be feared. But first you should learn what he, whom you resemble, wrote; for so you will be able to understand that those servants of God, whose companions we long to be found, resisted the sacrilege of Antiochus, just as we too, by God's favour, resist you. Holy scripture speaks, saying in the first book of Maccabees: 'And the king wrote to his whole kingdom, that the whole people should be one and that each should abandon his own laws. And all the nations accepted according to the word of the king, and many of Israel consented together with them and profaned the sabbath. And the king sent letters by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, that they should follow the laws of a foreign land, and forbid burnt offerings and sacrifice and libation in the sanctuary, defile the sabbaths and feast days, and profane the sanctuary, and set up shrines and idols, and sacrifice swine's flesh and common beasts, and leave their sons uncircumcised, and pollute their souls with every uncleanness and abomination, so that they might forget the law and change the ordinances; and whoever did not act according to the word of the king should die. According to all these words he sent writings to his whole kingdom and appointed overseers over the people. And he commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city. And many of the people gathered to them, everyone who forsook the law, and they did evil in the land.' And further on: 'And they built the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and in the cities of Judah round about they built altars, and at the doors of houses and in the streets they burned incense. And the books of the law which they found they tore up and burned with fire; and with whomever a book of the covenant was found, and if anyone consented to the law, the king's decree put him to death. In their power they did this to Israel, to those who were found, month by month, in the cities; and on the twenty-fourth of the month they sacrificed upon the altar which was upon the altar [of God]. And the women who had circumcised their children they put to death according to the command. They hung the infants from their necks, and [plundered] their houses, and [killed] those who had circumcised them. And many in Israel held firm and were strengthened in themselves not to eat common things, and they chose to die so as not to be defiled by foods and not to profane the holy covenant. And very great wrath came upon Israel in those days. And Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem, and he had five sons.' And further on: 'And they saw the blasphemies which were being done in Judah and in Israel, and he said: Woe is me, why was I born to see the ruin of the holy city, and to sit there while the sanctuary was given into the hand of enemies, into the hand of foreigners?' And further on: 'All her adornment has been taken away; from a free woman she has become a slave. See, our holy things and our beauty and our glory are laid waste, and the nations have profaned them. Why should we still live? And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments and covered themselves with sackcloth and mourned greatly. And those who were from the king came, and were compelling apostasy, to the city of Modein, so that they should sacrifice. And many of Israel went over to them. And Mattathias and his sons gathered together. And those who had been sent by the king answered and spoke to Mattathias, saying: You are a ruler, honoured and great in this city, and supported by sons and brothers. Now come forward first and carry out the king's command, as all the nations have done and the men of Judah and those left in Israel, and you and your sons will be friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honoured with silver and gold and many gifts. Mattathias answered and said with a loud voice: If all the nations in the king's dominion obey him, so that each departs from the service of his fathers, and they have chosen his commands, yet I and my sons will walk in the covenant of our fathers. The Lord be merciful to us; we will not forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hear the word of the king, we will not turn aside from the service of our worship to the right or to the left. When he had ceased speaking these words, a Jewish man came forward in the sight of all to sacrifice in Modein according to the king's command. And Mattathias saw it and was zealous, and his loins trembled, and he brought forth wrath according to judgment. And running to the altar he killed him. And the king's man who was compelling them to sacrifice he slew at that time, and he destroyed the altar. And he was zealous for the law, as Phinehas did to Zambri son of Salom. And Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying: Let everyone who is zealous, upholding the covenant, come out after me. And he and his sons fled into the mountains and left whatever they had in the city.'

What have you seen us do that is like this, that you see fit to say: 'Lucifer has insulted me'? He killed the king's officer with the sword, and also the man of his own people whom he had seen comply with the king's edict rather than God's. I, because I resist you and yours with words and say: 'I do not abandon the apostolic and evangelical faith; I believe as our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob believed,' am for that reason charged by you with insults. If you had fallen into the hands of this Mattathias, zealous for God, or into the hand of Phinehas, to whom God bears witness in Numbers through Moses, and you had tried to live after the manner of foreigners, they would without doubt have killed you with the sword. They would have been your killers with the sword. I, because with words I wound that mind of yours soaked in the blood of Christians, am judged by you guilty of insults. Why, emperor, do you not avenge yourself on me? Why do you not see fit to defend your honour against insult and to take vengeance on a beggarly man? Why are you not taking action? Not because you do not wish to, but because power has not yet been given to you by him to whom I am confident I belong, and so I say these things to you with a free voice, things which indeed seem to me depraved, in keeping with your abominable deeds. Since you see that we have renounced you and all the riches of your kingdom, and your father too, and you have observed that we have promised never in any way to depart from the faith, know that we greatly wonder that, though you are accustomed to devour with the edge of the sword those who displease you, you nevertheless spare us. I believe it is for the sake of piety, and we can well think this of your mildness. For I have been able to gather that, out of your excessive kindness, you have killed no one. You say: 'He is proud.' Why do I seem proud to you? Surely because you hear from me that you are doing what the enemies of God's religion have always done. It is my duty to press these things upon you, a heretic. Or are you not a heretic? But if you are a heretic, why do you accuse me of being injurious to you, when I am doing what God would not have me fail to do against you? The most holy prophet Jeremiah says that God said to him: 'And you, gird up your loins and rise and say all that I have commanded you, and do not fear before their face nor dread in their sight.' Since this is so, and the necessity of the duty laid on us by God presses us to say to you, as you act, whatever God has ordered to be said to you, it remains either that you obey God's commands when you are admonished by me, a servant and priest of his own clemency, or that you prove from the sacred Scriptures, perhaps on the ground that you are a king, that it is not lawful for me to admonish you in the name of the Lord so that you may correct yourself. If you cannot prove that it is forbidden to me, but rather begin to find that it is commanded me, that I should rebuke you and reprove and exhort and beseech and admonish you, and call you to please God, why do you say that I insult you? For he has given us, his bishops, power to rebuke and teach you who are entrusted to us to such a degree that he said: 'Do not fear before their face, do not dread in their sight. Behold, I have made you this day like a fortified city and like a strong wall of bronze against all the kings of Judah and its princes and the people of the land. And they will fight against you, and they will not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.' What are the things Jeremiah said to the kings of Judah and its princes and the peoples of the land? Surely these: that they had forsaken the Lord and sacrificed to foreign gods. These things you too have done and are doing: you have forsaken the apostolic and evangelical faith, you have taken up the Arian heresy, and you compel all the servants of God to become idolaters. Because you dare these things, you call proud those who desire to provide for your salvation. God says to Jeremiah: 'And you, gird up your loins and rise up, and say all that I say to you. Do not fear before their face nor dread in their sight.' And you, emperor Constantius, are indignant that we say to you in your error: 'Return to the way of salvation, abandon the error devised by Arius at the prompting of the devil.'

God commands that he alone is to be feared, and has enjoined that no one besides him is to be dreaded; and have you established things to be carried out that take away the fear of the Lord and make you to be dreaded? God says to Jeremiah: 'Behold, I have made you this day like a strong city and like a strong wall of bronze against all the kings of Judah and its princes and the people of the land. And they will fight against you and will not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord'; and do you suppose that you can be feared by any of the servants of God? Why do you call me arrogant and proud? Why do you call me insulting? Surely because I have found you by your works to be one of those of whom blessed John [says]: 'You have heard that antichrist is coming; but now there are many antichrists.' So you mark us out as guilty of injuries, as if we were the first to have resisted, so that you should not bring your idolatry into the church of God. You have read in the first book of Maccabees: 'And each man said to his neighbour: If we all do as our brothers have done and do not fight against the gentiles for our life and our ordinances, now they will very soon destroy us from the earth. And they took counsel on that day, saying: Every man, whoever comes against us in battle on the sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we shall not all die, as our brothers died in the hiding places. Then there gathered to them a company strong in might from Israel, everyone who was devoted to the law; and all who were fleeing from evils joined them and became a support to them. And they mustered a force and struck down the sinners in their anger and wicked men in their indignation. And the rest fled to the nations to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went round and destroyed the altars and circumcised by force the uncircumcised boys, as many as they found within the borders of Israel, and they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hand, and they recovered the law from the hands of the gentiles and of kings, and they did not give the horn to the sinner.' What does your mind, wounded by the poisons of Arius, see fit to think? What can your heart, torn by the bites of the serpent, devise against this defence of ours? When you observe that they did these things, should we have kept quiet while blasphemies were uttered by your mouth to wound the people divinely entrusted to us? 'And Mattathias,' it says, 'and his friends went round and destroyed the altars and circumcised by force the uncircumcised boys, as many as they found within the borders of Israel, and they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hand, and they recovered the law from the hands of the gentiles and of kings, and they did not give the horn to the sinner.' Since those who acted thus became most beloved of God, would it have been right for us, by flattering you and running with you in your crime, to become, as you are, most hostile to God? If we seem to you injurious on this account, because we could not accept your idolatry, give me, I ask, a single one among the worshippers of God who spared the adversaries of his religion. In the second book of Ezra, when people were speaking against their restoring the house and temple and city in Jerusalem to the Lord, [Nehemiah] says: 'The God of heaven himself has prospered us, and we his servants will rise and build; but you have no portion nor remembrance in Jerusalem'; and below, when the adversaries say: 'Will they sacrifice or eat in their place? Will not a fox go up and demolish their stone walls?', his servant Ezra says this to God: 'Hear, our God, for we have become despised, and turn their reproaches upon their own heads, and give them up to be a derision in a land of captivity; and do not cover their iniquity, and let their sins not be blotted out from before your face.'

What have we said of this kind concerning you? He to whom Ezra prayed is witness, he to whom I too pray and to whom my blessed church, established throughout the whole world, prays, that my wishes concerning you are these: that you correct your errors and become one of us. Observe meanwhile how the men of God neither feared their adversaries nor ceased from pouring out prayer against the enemies of God's house, so that, clearly, the forces of the adversaries of God's religion were brought to nothing. For so too the most holy Moses says to God in the song of Exodus: 'Let fear and trembling fall upon them at the greatness of your arm; let them become like stones until your people pass over, until your people pass over, O Lord, this people whom you have acquired.' Such words did they address to God concerning those handed over to them; we, because we say to you: 'Either turn to God, or be certain that God will bring all your empty pride to nothing,' seem to you insolent. Consider further what Mattathias did, that most holy man devoted to God, after those illustrious deeds he performed, and what he said to his sons at the end of his life, and see whether we, the priests of God, are not doing these things against you in right order. Holy Scripture speaks, saying: 'The days drew near for Mattathias to die, and he said to his sons: Now pride and chastisement have grown strong, and a time of overthrow and the wrath of indignation. Now, sons, be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers, and remember the works of the fathers which they did in their generations, and you will receive great glory and an everlasting name. Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness? Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment and became lord of Egypt. Phinehas our father, by being zealous with zeal, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Joshua, in fulfilling the word, became leader in Israel. Caleb, in bearing witness in the assembly, received an inheritance. David by his mercy obtained the throne of the kingdom for ever. Elijah, in being zealous with zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven. Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael, believing, were delivered from the flame. Daniel in his simplicity was delivered from the mouth of lions. And so consider from generation to generation that all who hope in him will not be made weak. And do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms. Today he is exalted, tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his thought will perish. Sons, be strong and prevail in the law, for in it you will be glorious. And behold Simeon your brother: I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him, he will be a father to you. And let Judas Maccabeus, strong in might from his youth, be the chief of your army, and he will fight the battle. And you shall bring to yourselves all the doers of the law, and avenge the vengeance of your people; repay the gentiles their repayment and pay heed to the commandment of the law.' When, therefore, you see that he gave such precepts to his sons and commanded those things to be done which he himself had also done, since he teaches that thus the patriarchs, the prophets and all the righteous pleased God, what did you want us to do, you dark one, so as not to seem defiant to you? Should we, the living, have yielded to you, a dead man, we servants of God to a henchman of the devil, when you see this Mattathias saying to his sons: 'And so consider from generation to generation that all who hope in him will not be made weak. And do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms. Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his thought will perish'? So as not to seem injurious to you, should we spare you as you destroy the house of God, you who are here today and tomorrow will be worms and dung, and so draw upon ourselves this offence before God, so that we deserve to be brought to nothing along with you?

Learn after this what the sons of that most devout Mattathias also did: whether they feared the hand of your fellow-executioner, whether they kept his army before their eyes and not our Lord, whom, believing him almighty as we believe, they [trusted as] they raised themselves against the enemy with all their strength. 'And Judas, who was called Maccabeus, his son, rose up in his place. And all his brothers helped him, and all who had joined themselves to his father; and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness. And he extended the glory of his people, and put on a breastplate like a giant, and girded on his weapons of war, and set battles in array, protecting the camp with the sword. And he became like a lion in his deeds, and like a lion's whelp roaring for prey. And he pursued the wicked, searching them out, and those who troubled his people he burned. And the wicked shrank back for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were thrown into confusion, and deliverance prospered in his hand. And he embittered many kings and delighted Jacob by his deeds, and his memory is blessed for ever. And he went through the cities of Judah and destroyed all the ungodly out of it, and turned away wrath from Israel. And he was renowned to the ends of the earth, and he gathered together those who were perishing.' They, kindled with such zeal, made [war] against the enemies of the house of God; were we not to have risen against you? Lest we be called insolent? But you would rightly call me insolent if we had not rightly despised your sacrilegious edict. For look at what the leaders of the Jews, your fellow-damned, commanded the apostles, and what, on the contrary, the choir of the blessed apostles did, and you will find that we are not insolent, but desire that both you and we be provided for. 'Now Peter and John were going up into the temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer. And a certain man, lame from his mother's womb, was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, so that he might ask alms from those entering the temple. When he saw Peter and John entering the temple, he asked for alms. And Peter, fixing his eyes on him with John, said: Look at us. And he looked at them, hoping to receive something from them.
