But Peter said to him: Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have, this I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise and walk. And taking him by his right hand he raised him up, and at once his feet and soles were made firm, and leaping up he stood and walked, and went into the temple with them, walking and leaping, praising God. And all the people saw him walking and praising God, and they recognised that he was the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him.' And below: 'As they were speaking these words to the people, the priests and the chief priest of the temple and the Sadducees rose up against them, grieved that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead, and they laid hands on them and put them in custody.' And below: 'Seeing the boldness of Peter and John, and having learned that they were unskilled men and without letters, they marvelled, recognising also that they had been with Jesus; and seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. And when they had ordered them to go out of the council, they conferred with one another, saying: What shall we do with these men? For that a sign has been done through them, known to all who live in Jerusalem, is manifest, and we cannot deny it. But so that these words may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them that they speak no more in this name to anyone. And when all agreed, they summoned them and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus. But Peter and John answered and said: Whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge; for we cannot but speak what we have seen and heard. And they, threatening them, let them go, finding no way to punish them because of the people; for all were glorifying God for what had happened. For the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old. And being released they came to their own and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them. And when they heard it, with one mind they raised their voice to the Lord and said: Lord, you are the God who made heaven and earth and sea and all that is in them, who through the Holy Spirit by the mouth of our father David your servant said: Why did the nations rage and the peoples devise vain things? The kings of the earth stood up and the princes gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. For truly there gathered together in this city against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed, Herod and Pontius Pilate with the nations and the peoples of Israel, to do what your hand and your counsel had foreordained. And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness, while you stretch out your hands for healings, and for signs and wonders to be done through the name of your holy Son Jesus. And when they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with all boldness.'

If you have now gathered all the reasons why we have brought these things forward, if you have thoroughly absorbed the whole intent of our argument, will you dare to say any longer that we are insolent? For you see that the blessed apostles neither yielded to the leaders of the Jews nor gave way to their threats, but rather always fearlessly carried into effect what had been entrusted to them; and likewise that the people of God not only were not terrified by the threats of the unbelievers, but even prayed that God would deign to grant his apostles boldness in speaking and steadfastness in defending the truth. If, then, this was done both by the blessed apostles and by the peoples dedicated to God, and they were not called either defiant or insolent by God because they resisted his enemies, how is it that we are called by you proud, insolent, insulting, we who, though sinners, nevertheless hold the holy faith of the apostles and of those peoples who believed in the only Son of God? [We are called] proud along with the apostles for this reason: because we, soldiers of Christ, count as nothing your voice, an apostate's, and your terrors, a sacrilegious man's; because we proclaim the Son of God as the true Son of God, just as the most blessed apostles proclaimed him. So we seem to you shameless, insolent, proud, as the most holy apostles seemed to the Jews, to whom, had they been in the body today, you could have said these things which you deign to say to us. For we find that they were always commanded, by the mouth of your fellow-blasphemers, the scribes, the Pharisees, the rulers and the chief priest of the Jews, not to teach or preach the only Son of God; yet hear further what is written of what they did, in case your heart, fattened with darkness, can perhaps at some time be brought to see the truth: 'By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all of one mind in Solomon's portico, but of the rest no one dared to join them, yet the people magnified them. And more and more believers were added to the Lord, multitudes of men and women, so that they carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and pallets, so that when Peter came even his shadow might fall on some of them. And they were freed from their infirmity. And a multitude from the cities around Jerusalem also came together, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and all were healed. But the chief priest rose up, and all who were with him, of the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with envy and laid hands on the apostles and put them in custody. But an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison and led them out, saying: Go, and standing in the temple speak to the people all the words of this life. And when they heard this, they went into the temple at daybreak and taught. And the chief priest and those with him came and called together the council and all the assembly of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought. But the officers came and did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported, saying: We found the prison shut with all care and the guards standing at the door; but when we opened it we found no one inside. When the rulers and the chief priest heard these words, they were perplexed about them, what this might be. But someone came and reported to them, saying: Look, the men whom you put in custody are standing in the temple and teaching the people. Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not by force; for they feared the people, lest they be stoned. And when they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the priest questioned them, saying: We strictly charged you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and you want to bring that man's blood upon us. But Peter and the apostles answered, saying: Must one obey God or men?' If, then, God must be obeyed and not men, why do you call us defiant, why do you call us injurious, when you see that we obey the commands of God? 'When they heard this, they were furious,' says Scripture, 'and they planned to kill them.' So you too hold us in custody and threaten to kill us, because you are possessed by that spirit by which the Jews were held captive and are still held. If you are not held captive by that unclean spirit, why do you forbid us to confess and preach the only Son of God? The angel of God, leading the apostles out of the prison of the Jews, your fellow-desperates, [says]: 'Go, teach in the temple the words of this life'; and you, taking priests from the church of God, have thought they should be thrown into prison, so that we should not preach the word of life.

Meanwhile, I beg you to answer what difference there is between you and your fellow-Scotinus, whom the people of Sirmium, reversing the sense, call Photinus. You are asked to distinguish what the difference is, how far apart you stand. Look: if at that time the rulers and the high priest and the whole council of the Jews said to the apostles, 'You want to bring that man's blood upon us,' Photinus too professes the Son of God to be only a man, and says that he did not exist before the blessed Mary. Yours also is this profession: that the Son of God does indeed exist before all things, that is, before the heavens, the earth, the sea and all that is in them, but that he came into being out of nothing, and that he is a creature. What difference do you think there is between you and Paul of Samosata, or that disciple of his, your fellow-Scotinus, except that you say 'before all things,' and he 'after all things'? For the rest, you have one mind of cruelty and unbelief, so as to say that God does not have a true Son. See, on the other hand, how the holy Church believes. We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of things visible and invisible, and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, born of the Father, that is, of the substance of the Father, God from God, light from light, true God from true God, born not made, of one substance with the Father, which the Greeks call *homoousion*, through whom all things were made, whether in heaven or on earth, who for us men and for our salvation came down, was made flesh, became man, suffered, rose again on the third day, ascended into heaven, and will come to judge the living and the dead; and we believe also in the Holy Spirit. You see that this is the apostolic and evangelical faith, which maintains that the Son has always reigned and reigns with the Father, which confesses both that the divine Trinity is perfect and that it has one substance. Otherwise, what difference would there be between the Church and you heretics, or the Jews, if the blessed Church did not believe thus? What [would be] the holy faith? So that you might know what the Church of the Lord punishes in you, she has said and says of you: 'But those who say: There was when he was not, and before he was born he was not, and that he was made out of things that did not exist, or from another substance, saying that the Son of God is mutable and changeable, these the catholic and apostolic Church anathematizes.' For this holy faith the apostles were shut up in prison, received chains, were tormented with beatings hour after hour, so that they should not reveal the truth to the world; and yet they would not refrain from preaching, even to the point of being slaughtered. And you say that we are men of the greatest defiance, because, that is, we keep to the way of the apostles, because we tell you that you have gone astray, [as] the blessed John the Baptist did to Herod. 'But Herod the tetrarch, when he was rebuked by him on account of Herodias, his brother's wife, and for all the evils that Herod had done, added this above all, and shut John up in prison.' For what reason did Herod shut John up? Surely because his deeds were being exposed. So you too deal with the servants of God, because we say to you: Do not do what you are doing, do not be a murderer, do not persecute the Church of the Lord, do not reject the apostolic faith and approve the heretical, do not bring idolatry into the Church. We consider that we say these things specially for your salvation; and if you refuse to restrain yourself, without doubt you will be seeking eternal death for yourself, just as Herod also sought it; for he could not harm John, whether by throwing him into prison or by killing him, since you see that John is the friend of God, but Herod the enemy of God. Seeking to harm us, who long for eternal safety to be granted you, you persecute us in every way; but the powers of your authority will not be able to prevail to harm the servants of the only Son of God, because you are found to be one of those whom he made subject to us believers, saying: 'Look, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and over all the strength of the enemy; and nothing shall harm you.' You who call me proud because I tell you the truth, what do you want me to be found? That servant who received one talent and hid it and presented that alone to his master, and, because he did not present it to his master multiplied by interest as his fellow-servants did, deserved even to lose that talent and to hear: 'Wicked and lazy servant'? Or the one who presented the sum he received multiplied tenfold, and to whom it was said: 'Well done, good and faithful servant; because you were faithful in a little, I will also set you over much; enter into the joy of your master'? But how shall I be able to hear that, if out of fear of you I do what pleases you? Look in the Gospel at what the Lord wished us to do, and stop calling us arrogant: 'There was a certain rich man; he went away into a distant country to receive a kingdom and to return. And he called ten servants and gave them ten talents and said to them: Trade until I come. But his citizens hated him and sent an embassy after him, saying: We do not want this man to reign over us. And it happened, when he returned, having received the kingdom, that he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be called, so that he might know how much each had gained by trading. The first came, saying: Lord, your talent has gained ten talents. And he said to him: Well done, good servant; because you were faithful in a little, you will have authority over ten cities. And another came, saying: Lord, your mina has made five talents. And he said to this one too: You, be over five cities. And another came, saying: Here is your talent, which I kept laid up in a napkin, because I feared you, since you are a severe man; you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow. And the master said to him: Out of your own mouth I judge you, faithless servant; you knew that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow; then why did you not put my money on the bankers' table, so that on coming I might have collected it with interest? And to those standing by [he said]: Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents. And I say to you: to everyone who has, it will be given; but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away. But those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and kill them before me.'

Surely, if you do not change yourself, you will be one of those who were ordered to be killed. That is why I seem proud to you: because I desire you not to be killed, because I long for you too to be found in that sum entrusted to me which I desire to be multiplied. Because we wage our struggle with you in this way, we seem enemies to you, we who, keeping the precept of the blessed apostle, pour out prayer unceasingly for your safety: 'I urge, then, first of all, that supplications, prayers, petitions and thanksgivings be made for all men, for kings and all who are in high station, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life with godliness and gravity. For this is good and acceptable before God our Saviour, who wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.' We, who desire you to attain the knowledge of the truth, seem enemies to you; you call me insulting because I say what serves your salvation and mine. But this assertion of yours too, which claims that I do you injury, shows you to be imprudent. For if you had been prudent, first, you would never have been found sacrilegious; then, rebuked by the authority of the sacred Scriptures, you would already have shown yourself a restrained man. But now, because you are imprudent, when a bishop says to you, 'Emperor, look to your salvation, for you are weighed down by the huge burdens of your crimes,' you say: 'You insult me.' 'I charge you before God,' says the apostle to Timothy, 'and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, that you keep these things without discrimination, doing nothing by partiality'; but [you say I should] keep fairness [toward you]. And you call him insulting who, finding you caught in such great crimes, now rebukes you for having committed them, now entreats you to rescue yourself from your evils while there is opportunity, and to be such a one as God will not punish among those whom he marks out as worthless and faithless, saying: 'I have begotten sons and exalted them, but they have despised me.' That is why I seem proud to you: because I desire you to be found among those whom the only Son of God invites to his kingdom, saying: 'Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world.' You think you suffer insult because what is true is said to you; the glorious apostle, on the contrary, commands, saying: 'Rebuke sinners before all, so that the rest also may have fear.' Whom ought I to heed? You, who say: 'Allow me to destroy the religion of God, to turn his servants to Antichrist, allow me to establish everyone in this sacrilege of mine'? Or the blessed apostle, who instructs me to rebuke you, a sinner, before all? But if you think I ought to have spared you because you are emperor, in this too you are found imprudent. For you hear the apostle say: 'Rebuke sinners before all, so that the rest also may have fear'; and you say: 'You ought to have spared me especially, because I was king of the Roman empire.' And where would I be leaving out this charge: 'I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, that you keep these things without discrimination, doing nothing by leaning to one side'? That, surely, is why I seem to you to be insulting: because I have not put your commands before the commands of God. In the Acts of the Apostles I read that the blessed apostles were seized by those whose partner you are not only in unbelief but also in cruelty, and that they were commanded not to teach in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. But let us look together at that very part of sacred Scripture, [to see] whether the apostles yielded to the commands of the enemies of the only Son of God, or most earnestly carried through what they had undertaken to fulfil. 'Calling the apostles,' it says, 'they beat them and released them, commanding them not to speak to anyone in the name of Jesus. So they went rejoicing from the presence of the council, because they had been counted worthy to suffer insult for the name. And every day, in the temple and at home, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ.'

Since sacred Scripture reports that the blessed apostles acted thus, are we, the appointed overseers of God's churches, to keep silent while you invite the hearts of all to deny the Son of God and busy yourself with establishing your heresy, so that, evidently, we may not be found to have been insulting to you, a blasphemer, a murderer, a destroyer of God's religion? Sacred Scripture says that the apostles feared neither the blows nor the threats of the sons of pestilence, but always taught; were we to be broken by the force of your perishable reign, so that you could carry out all your wicked attempts? We are judged stubborn by you because true things are told you by us. So too your fellow-blasphemers condemned the most blessed Stephen, because he said to them: 'Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you have always resisted the Holy Spirit; as your fathers [did], so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced the coming of the Just One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become, you who received the law by the ordering of angels and did not keep it.' When the Jews heard these things, were they rightly stirred against the most holy martyr Stephen, or wrongly? If wrongly, then see that you too are wrongly stirred against those who want you saved. Notice that you stand against the Church of God on that side on which the Jews stood then and are standing now; that you are thus stiff-necked, thus uncircumcised in heart and ears; that is why, just as they, hearing true things, did not endure them but rushed to kill a worshipper of God, you too are rushing to kill us who tell you things sound and plain. 'Now when they heard these things,' says divine Scripture, 'they raged in their hearts and gnashed their teeth at him'; and below: 'And crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed at him with one mind, and having cast him out of the city they stoned him.' So you, raging in heart and gnashing your teeth, are against us for no other reason than that we call you a persecutor of God's house, a destroyer of God's religion, a shedder of the blood of Christ's servants, that we rightly name you sacrilegious, since [you are] a blaspheming heretic, since [you are] one who assails the apostolic and evangelical faith. We do nothing hateful to God if, dealing with you in this manner, we tell you what we understand you to be. For we find that men such as you are acted thus against the glorious. 'And as they were ministering,' says Scripture, 'and fasting to the Lord, the Holy Spirit said: Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them. Then, fasting and praying, they laid hands on them and sent them off. And they, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus. And when they had come to Salamis, they preached the word of the Lord in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John as assistant. And when they had gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a Jewish false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus, which is interpreted "Ready", who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; he, having summoned Barnabas and Saul, sought to hear the word of God. But Etoemus the magician (for so his name is said to be interpreted) opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith. But Saul, who is Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixing his eyes on him, said: O full of all deceit and fraud, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, you do not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord. And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is against you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time. And at once mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about he sought someone to lead him by the hand. Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, amazed with wonder at the teaching of the Lord.' We believe that, instructed by this testimony, you will not say: 'Lucifer insults me, the emperor.'

What does it matter to me what you are, since I say these things which he heard from the apostle who was recognised to have been a false prophet? For do I not regard you, the emperor Constantius, just as the glorious Paul and Barnabas regarded Bar-Jesus the Jew? For you are found to be opposed to the name of the Lord just as he was; you resist the truth as he resisted it; you do not want men to believe in the only Son of God, [but] to believe you and that Jewish false prophet, only because you are driven by a hostile spirit just as he was driven. For when you hear that the proconsul was a prudent man and desired to be instructed by the blessed apostles, so that he might grasp the way of truth, and that he whose imitator you are resisted the apostles, so that they should not lead the proconsul to believe in the Son of God, it is plain that you are such as that Jewish false prophet was. Likewise, since holy Scripture says that Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, uttered that invective, you ought to understand that that Jewish false prophet was full of an unclean spirit. So, just as he, driven by a hostile spirit, spoke against [them], since you too are found to resist in this way at the prompting of the Adversary, you must judge yourself to be none other than Bar-Jesus the Jewish false prophet. Therefore, since you understand that you are a second Bar-Jesus, a Jewish false prophet, as often as it has been said by your sacrilegious mouth, 'God has no true Son', do not take it ill if we say to you the things that were said by the apostle to your predecessor the Jewish false prophet: 'full of all deceit and fraud, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, who do not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord.' If you are stirred [to ask] why the things are said to you that were said to him whose road of death you are following, you will show yourself very foolish, wanting to be what that son, the Jewish false prophet, was, and not wanting to be called by the names by which he too was called. Again I both urge and beseech, as I also warn, that you be willing to take thought for yourself, so that eternal punishment may not receive you. For if he deserved to be blinded thus because he tried to resist, consider what evils can be set before you, a murderer, a sacrilegious man, a destroyer of God's religion, both in this life and for ever. Take further the things that can teach you that we are not insulting, but truthful. Those seven most glorious brothers resisted Antiochus, just as we now have resisted you. You have read what the fourth answered your fellow-pestilence, you who deign to keep crying out that I am insulting because I tell you that unless you are converted to God you will perish for ever; for he says: 'It is better, being given over to death by men, to await from God the hope of being raised again by him; for you there will be no resurrection to life.' If you, a tyrant, hear from us that you will not receive the resurrection to life if you remain in this unbelief, that you will rise not to rest but to everlasting punishment, what insult is that? Scripture says too that the fifth, when he had been brought forward and tortured, said to the king: 'You have power among men, though you are corruptible; you do what you will; but do not think that our race has been abandoned by God. Wait patiently and see how his great power will torment you and your seed.' What do you think, since with such constancy the servant of God inveighed against your fellow-tyrant? Will you, a worshipper of the devil, judge the worshipper of God to have been abusive? You will deny that he was arrogant in speaking true things; nor should you judge me insolent because I tell you that we are not abandoned by God, for whose sake I endure these things, while you, on the contrary, unless you are corrected, will come to nothing with your corruptible glory. Look also at what the sixth said, and you will find that we strive against you, a turbulent storm, in the same formation in which they strove: 'Do not err in vain; for we suffer these things on our own account, having sinned against our God, and they have been done as a fitting admonition; but do not think that you will go unpunished, since you have tried to fight against God.' The letters of my humble self and my books, though written in rustic language, prove that I have often said that our sins indeed brought it about that we came into your hands, you forerunner of Antichrist, but that you nonetheless are fighting against God, and therefore, unless you look to yourself, you will, like that Antiochus, go into eternal punishment, whereas the Lord will be merciful to us.

You are aggrieved that we reveal to those entrusted to us both you and who you are, and that it is fitting that you, the shadow of Antichrist, be trampled by all the soldiers of Christ. 'Who,' you say, 'have been able to trample me?' Those whom, because they confess themselves Christians, you keep shut up in prisons, deprive of their patrimony, drive into exile, torture, kill. Hence you judge us insolent, because we beseech all entrusted to us to trample the devil's head, to bring your sacrilegious attempts to nothing by the power of the sufferings inflicted on them for Christ, the only Son of God. Let that most glorious mother of these seven sons also be insolent in your eyes, because she deigned to entice her sons to conquer your fellow-madman Antiochus, saying: 'I do not know how you appeared in my womb, nor did I give you breath and life, nor did I myself put together the limbs of each of you; but the Creator of the world, who formed the birth of man and who searches out the origin of all things, will in his mercy give you back both breath and life, as you now disregard yourselves for the sake of his laws.' The devout mother did not cease to say these things to her sons, loving her sons bravely, until she saw them all killed. Were we, by contrast, whom he had foretold by the mouth of the prophet as the future shepherds of his flock, saying, 'And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will feed you, feeding [you] with discipline', to keep silent, so that we might not seem insolent to you, a raging wolf coming to slaughter God's sheep? A woman so kindled her sons' hearts with the love of God that by their death she won the victories of the sword; and you have thought it fitting for us to say to Christ's soldiers: 'Do not take up arms against Constantius, the devil's henchman; do not resist the temple of all demons; rather, do whatever he commands to be done.' What is this stubbornness of ours, if we strive to fulfil the office delegated to us by God, if, in short, we are found to be imitators of that woman? You want to please the devil, whose work you are found to perform; you do not at all want us, by acting against you in these things, to become most acceptable to God. If it still moves you that you are called those things by us, take also what that seventh son of this woman cried out thus against Antiochus: 'But Antiochus, thinking himself scorned and despising the voice of her who reproached [him], while the youngest still survived, not only exhorted him with words but also affirmed with an oath that he would make him rich and happy, would transfer him from his ancestral ways, would have him as a friend, and would entrust him with affairs of state. But as the youth paid no heed to this, he called the mother and urged her to become [the means] of the youth's safety. And when he had exhorted her with many words, she undertook to persuade her son. So, bending towards him, she mocked the cruel tyrant and said in her ancestral tongue: Son, have pity on me, who carried you in my womb for ten months, and gave you milk for three years, and nourished you and brought you to this age. I beg you, child, look at heaven and earth, and having observed all that is in them, understand that God made them out of nothing, and that the human race comes to be thus, so that you may not fear this executioner, but, proving worthy of your brothers, may accept death, so that in that mercy he may receive you back with your brothers. When she had said this, the youth said: Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the king's command, but I obey the precept of the law, which was given to us through Moses. But you, who have become the inventor of all malice against the Hebrews, will not escape the hand of God. For if, for the sake of rebuke and correction, our Lord is a little angry with us while we live, yet he will be reconciled again to his servants. And you, O wicked man and most shameful of all men, do not vainly exalt yourself, puffed up with empty hopes against his servants; for you have not yet escaped the judgement of the almighty God who sees all things. For our brothers, having now endured brief pain, have fallen under God's covenant of eternal life; but you, by the judgement of God, will pay the just penalties of your pride. And I, like my brothers, give up both soul and body for our ancestral laws, calling on God to become merciful to our nation soon, and [to make] you confess with torments and blows that he alone is God. And in me and in my brothers the wrath of the Almighty will come to rest, which has justly been brought upon our whole nation.'

What more, Constantius, have you heard from us than what was said by this faithful servant of God? If he said to Antiochus' henchmen: 'Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the king's command, but I obey the precept of the law which was given to us through Moses', we too say to yours: 'Why do you think that you can make us Arians at the will of Constantius, the forerunner of Antichrist? As we are Christians, so we shall always be.' If he said to Antiochus: 'But you, who have become the inventor of all malice against the Hebrews, will not escape the hand of God', we too have said to you, and are saying, that since there has never been any persecutor of the sacred law of God greater than you, you will not escape the hand of God. If Antiochus heard that the Lord was then angry with his own people for the sake of reproving them, and that he would be reconciled again to his servants, you too hear us saying these things. If it was said to that king: 'And you, O wicked man and most shameful of all men, do not vainly exalt yourself, puffed up with empty hope against his servants; for you have not yet escaped the judgement of the almighty God who sees all things', you too hear these things from us: that you are wicked, the most shameful of all men, who do these things in order to make us your fellow-apostates, but that you are nevertheless exalted in vain, puffed up by the devil's prompting with empty hope against us, the servants of God, because you can neither accomplish your malicious attempts nor escape the judgement of God who sees all things and has power over all things. You hear from us, just as Antiochus heard through that illustrious young man, that our brothers, having endured a little, have fallen under God's covenant of eternal life, but that you, by the judgement of God, will pay the just penalties of your pride. You hear from us too that we are ready to be killed by you, the executioner, for God's sake, just as you have already killed our brothers, that we are ready to give up our souls and bodies for Jesus Christ, the true and only Son of God; and moreover that we trust in his untiring goodness, that he will soon rescue his whole flock from you, the ravening wolf, from you, the rabid dog; but that you, unless you take thought for yourself, will depart into everlasting torments. Whatever more I have said to you, whether in writing or face to face, I want you to refute it, you tyrant of our time. If I have called you an executioner, not only did this most righteous young man say it, but also his mother, to Antiochus, your fellow-madman; if you have been called by me the inventor of all malice, if [I have said] that you will not escape the hand of God, if [I have called you] wicked and the most shameful of all men, because you will not escape the judgement of him who is almighty and sees all things, but will pay the just penalties in the judgement of God, all these things had already been said by this devout young man to your colleague Antiochus. You keep crying out that I am insulting, because you see names fitting your deeds laid upon you, those which our predecessors, the worshippers of the living God, already laid upon your fellow-tyrants. The blessed apostle Peter says: 'Be sober, be watchful; your adversary the devil, like a roaring lion, goes about seeking whom he may devour; resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that your brotherhood throughout this whole world endures these same sufferings.' If you think that I am insulting because you hear that what you do is evil, in what then am I found resisting the devil according to the apostle's precept? For see, this dragon, leading you with his wine into utter drunkenness, has sent you against the whole flock of God, so that, using your royal support, you may make all men drunk as you yourself are, that is, insane, senseless and demented. For has he not made you so drunk from the vine of Sodom, from the vineyard of Gomorrah, that you did not see that you had committed fornication, just as the Jews committed fornication? In what, I say, shall we resist the devil, if no one goes out to meet you, through whom he has armed himself to devour us? If it is not said to you, the drunkard, by the sober, to you, the sick man, by the healthy, to you, the wounded, by the whole, to you, the blind, by those who see, to you, the fallen, by those who stand, to you, the impious, by the pious, to you, the ravening wolf, by the sheep of God, to you, the cruel executioner and savage murderer, by the most kindly and those who love mercy, to you, the blasphemer, by those who glorify God, to you, the sacrilegist, by the worshippers of God, to you, the Arian heretic, by Christians, if it is not said to you by us: 'Depart, servant of our adversary; give honour to God'? In what shall we resist the devil if we spare you, the net of his will, if your drunkenness, that is, your insanity, is not declared to all, if, finally, through the fact that you rage against us, it is not made manifest to the whole world that from your doing these things you cannot be perceived as a servant of Christ, but plainly as the slave of him who is like a roaring lion against us? Hence we seem to you to be insolent, because we tell you that you have been made drunk with that wine by which they too were led into all the madness of drunkenness, those to whom or about whom it is said: 'They have sinned, not his, stained children; a crooked and perverse generation, is this what you have repaid the Lord? Thus, a foolish and unwise people?' And below: 'Jacob drank wine and ate and was filled, and the beloved kicked; he grew fat and became gross, he grew broad and forsook God who made him, and departed from God his saviour. They provoked me with strange [gods], with their abominations they roused me, and they sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know; new ones came lately, whom their fathers did not know. You forsook the God who begot you, and forgot the God who nourishes you.' So your faithlessness, which you preach, proves that you, like the Jews, have forsaken God and followed idolatry.

But now I have judged that you should be brought to this one point only, that you might see that we are not abusive, insolent and arrogant because I tell you what you are, but truthful, and fearing no one except God. When the most blessed apostle John says: 'Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out', you seem to me plainly to be one of these false prophets, since by denying the only Son of God you declare that you have nothing in your sacrilegious mouth but the spirit of Antichrist. Hence it comes about that you cannot even listen to us speaking of the divine eternity of the only Son of God, since that spirit of Antichrist which dwells in you cannot bear it and does not want to be driven out of you, but desires to keep dwelling in you until it sees you snatched away to those places in which it will itself be for ever; for it grieves that you, its most faithful darling, you who obey all its desires, should be torn from it. 'Beloved,' he says, 'do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this know the Spirit of God: every spirit which confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God. And every spirit which destroys Jesus is not from God, and this is that [spirit] of Antichrist.' And below: 'They are of the world, therefore they speak of the world and the world hears them; but we are from God. He who knows God hears us; but he who is not from God does not hear us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.' It is clear, Constantius, that you carry the spirit of Antichrist, that you are driven by the spirit of error. For just as those who said that the only Son of God did not take on a man from the womb of the blessed Virgin, who did not believe that he was incarnate and made man, are shown to have the spirit of error and are called [spirits] of Antichrist, so you Arians too, when you deny that the only Son of God was truly born of the Father, that is, of the substance of the Father, when you spurn [the faith] that he is the true Son and has always reigned with the Father, when you refuse to believe that the Son was never without the Father nor the Father without the Son, when you deny that the Father and his only Son have one Godhead, whose spirit do you show yourselves to be full of, if not that of Antichrist? For one who has the Spirit of God cannot say of the only Son of God, 'There was when he was not, and he was made from nothing', since he believes that he has reigned with the Father without beginning and will reign without end. Therefore, when you say that he is not the true Son of God, and when, finally, you try to destroy [the faith] that he is homoousion, as the Greeks say, while we Romans say 'of one substance with the Father', you certainly declare yourselves too to be of those false prophets and among the antichrists.

You ought not to judge me insulting because I say that you are driven by an unclean spirit, because I say that you are a forerunner of Antichrist; for your own mouth reveals that you are this, and no one who has the Spirit of God could assert such things as you Arians maintain, or all your fellow-heretics of various sects. You deny that God has a true Son, you say that he is adopted, and you suppose that you are not understood, namely that you are one of those antichrists, as John declares with his own mouth. You have been exposed, I say, as led by a hostile spirit. That, in short, is why we did not believe you when you said of the Son: 'He was made from nothing.' For we knew that these things could be said only by the spirit of a false prophet, only by a forerunner of Antichrist, only by an attendant and slave of demons. We could not have believed you when you said these things, since the Holy Spirit spoke through the prophets too about the only Son of God, that he is the true Son of God, that he is eternal and co-eternal with the Father, that neither was the Son ever without the Father nor was or is the Father without the Son; and the blessed apostles reported these same things, since the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, who was in the prophets, also abode in the apostles. And since this holy Spirit the Paraclete is in the Church of God, and you are placed outside the Church of God, as he does not abide in you, you are certainly proved to have the spirit of Antichrist; and this unclean spirit, so that you may not see the things we press upon you, pours darkness over your heretical hearts with the blind fog of errors, so that, of course, you may not be able to escape from his snares. You judge us insulting because we declare you to be such as we see you are. Look: when I find that the Lord said in the Gospel according to Matthew, 'Behold, I send you as sheep among wolves', you seem to me to be one of those wolves, and indeed one in whom I see heaped together the rage of all the wolves roaring against the flock of God. For what denier of the only Son of God would not rejoice, would not make a show of it, when he sees that you have so ravaged the flock of Christ? I also take you to be one of those unbelievers, one of those faithless ones to whom it is said: 'Brood of vipers, how can you speak what is good when you are evil? For each one speaks from his mouth out of the abundance of the heart. The good man brings forth good things out of a good treasure, and the evil man brings out evil things out of an evil treasure.' If the things you speak are good, Constantius, you may have a good treasure. I am insolent because I tell you that darkness dwells in your heart; hence, from your utterly darkened mind, being what you are, you dare to bring forth unclean and dark things. Look, if you hear also what was said to blessed Peter by the Lord, you will without doubt call me insulting. The most holy Matthew says: 'While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people; and he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying: "Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him." And at once he came up to Jesus and said: "Hail, Rabbi." And he kissed him. But Jesus said: "Friend, why have you come?" Then they came up and laid hands on Jesus and seized him. And behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the servant of the chief priest and cut off his ear. Then Jesus said to him: "Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword shall perish by the sword."' You must call me insulting when you hear that, if you use the sword, you are to perish by the sword. Or have you not used the sword? If you have killed none of the Christians with the sword, if you have persecuted none to the point of death because he confessed the only Son of God to be the true Son, because he held the apostolic and evangelical faith, because he refused to be an Arian, then you may not perish by the sword. For you hear it said to blessed Peter, and indeed by God, the only Son of God, that everyone who uses the sword is to perish by the sword. I am insulting because I have told you: Christians may not kill, because it befits Christians to suffer injury, not to do it, [even] to be killed; for you ought, for Christ's sake, not to kill those who proclaim themselves Christians. These commandments the Lord gave us; if they are kept, then we shall persevere in being Christians. You, on the contrary, since you see fit to pursue his servants with the sword, we certainly can no longer call a Christian, but plainly a brigand or a gladiator.

Meanwhile, since we have recited how your fellow-madman Judas Iscariot betrayed the Lord, let us at this point thoroughly re-examine the causes of his sacrilege and of yours, and you will find that you are one, you and Judas Iscariot. He betrayed the Lord to the Jews because he had not been a believer, except in the way your fellow-Scotinus of the people of Sirmium, who was and is unworthily called Photinus, is now a believer. You have betrayed him, and indeed to the whole world, so that all may deny his divinity. Which of you is the greater in crime? I think that you are. For 'everyone who sins against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither here nor in the future.' You have stood forth as the betrayer of his Godhead, so that all may deny it. For, as far as lies in you, you have betrayed him, about whom you have both issued written books and set up preachers of your kindly wish in every place. So that all might deny that he is the true Son of God, you caused the apostolic and evangelical faith, written out against you heretics at Nicaea, to be judged heretical, and you caused your blasphemy to be called catholic. And yet this Judas who had betrayed him, seeing that he had wrought the death of his own salvation, was moved by repentance and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying: 'I have sinned in betraying righteous blood.' But they said: 'What is that to us? See to it yourself.' And throwing the silver into the temple he withdrew, went away and hanged himself with a noose. He, though only for a moment, repented and returned the price he had received; what have you done like this, you who, when admonished by his servants that you were committing a crime, not only did not repent but grew rather in obstinacy? What have you done like this, you who are giving all the resources of your kingdom so that you may establish your sacrilege, who have corrupted some by the huge reward of your wealth, those whom you could not corrupt from the truth in another way, who have so enriched a certain number of needy men that they can be equalled with your counts in the greatness of their riches? Judas, after he perceived his crime, ended his life with a noose; you, who for the greatness of your evil-doing deserve to be punished with a greater penalty, what will you do when you come to know, though late, that you have done wrong, when your eyes, festering with heretical poison, begin to see the things which they can now by no means perceive? And yet, if you are willing to believe, what you do out of ignorance must be forgiven you, just as you observe that it was forgiven the blessed apostle Paul; but if not, you will go down like Judas into the night of hell, and then you will say to those who now drove you to do these things, that is, to your fellow-Arians: 'I have sinned with you, denying the only Son of God; I have sinned in granting you authority to deny his eternal clemency.' Then, when you begin to recognise that we rightly confess one eternity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, when you begin to see that there is one greatness and one power in the Father and in his only Son and in the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, where then will they be who drove you to commit this sacrilege, so that you say to them: 'I repent that I ran with you, enemies of God, that with you I persecuted the house of God'? They will without doubt be with you in Gehenna. Where then will be the riches of your kingdom, which serve you not for salvation but for your eternal destruction? We do indeed pray that God may see fit to reveal the truth to you, the enemy of your own salvation, and that you may escape from such great dangers. For the rest, how far you surpass Judas Iscariot in crime is no labour to judge, since you have summoned the whole world to deny his divinity, whereas Judas betrayed the Lord only to those who had not yet believed in him; you, on the contrary, have seen fit to provoke even those who had already believed to deny his Godhead. Judas used force on no one to make him perish with him; you, on the contrary, fight with an armed band of soldiers against us, whom you know to believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed; certainly it is no great labour to weigh how far apart you and Judas stand.

You call me insulting because I desire that both I and those entrusted to me should not be wounded by your pestilent teaching, because I tell you that you are full of disease and therefore must be avoided by the servants of God, lest we ourselves, made diseased, perish together with you in this plague of yours. 'Would that you would bear with a little of my foolishness,' the apostle says to the Corinthians, 'but do bear with me. For I am jealous for you with the jealousy of God. For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear lest, as the serpent seduced Eve by his cunning, your minds be corrupted from the chastity that is in Christ Jesus.' That is why I seem to you insulting: because I fear lest through your blasphemy you corrupt the chastity which we have in Christ Jesus, because we are afraid lest, as your dearest serpent seduced Eve by his cunning, you seduce us from God and make us liable to death. You call me obstinate because I say that you are a deceitful worker, a false Christian. These things are not first brought against you by me. For you hear that the blessed apostle designated you a deceitful worker, a false apostle: 'For such false apostles are deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ. And no wonder, for Satan himself transforms himself as an angel of light; it is no great thing if his ministers transform themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.' Hence I seem to you proud, because, knowing it from your deeds, I say that you are one of those whom the Holy Spirit foretold through the apostle would be such. If you are not a deceitful worker, refute me; for I know that you pretend to be a Christian, though you are an Arian, and that you have wanted to make all of us servants of him whose attendant you are. If you are not a deceitful worker, prove it; for we see you feigning piety in certain matters, while you exercise all your impiety against us Christians. If you are not a deceitful worker, how is it that, pretending to establish peace, you had striven to destroy the whole Church of God, to dissolve the peace handed down to it through the only Son of God? For I could not have the peace of the Lord from the moment I had done what you ordered me against the Lord's command, from the moment, in short, I had begun to deny the only Son of God himself, as you deny him. If you are not transformed into the apostles of Christ, why are you as anxious as if the whole care of the Church truly belonged to you, namely that no catholic bishop should preside over a church anywhere, that no one should be left who could confess himself a Christian? You remove catholic bishops, you ordain heretics, you write dreadful threats, lest by chance sedition should arise. Certainly whoever does not know supposes, while he sees you doing these things, that you are a Christian; we, on the contrary, who, instructed by the apostle, happily know that Satan has transformed himself as an angel of light, Satan who carries out all these things against the holy Church through you, cannot wonder if we see you as his minister, if we see a minister of unrighteousness transformed as though [a minister] of righteousness. We exhort you: would that you might turn yourself to this, so that you can be believed a servant of God, so that you can be judged and understood a Christian. As often as we tell you that you could not have become a denier of the only Son of God unless you were full of a hostile spirit, you are accustomed to say that we do you injury; and although I have already proved this point in very many places, that you come against the household of God with unclean spirits goading your hearts, take further what happened in the Acts of the Apostles: 'It came to pass, as we were going to prayer, that a certain girl having a spirit of Python met us, who brought her masters much profit by divining. She followed Paul and us and cried out, saying: "These men are servants of the most high God, who proclaim to us the way of salvation." And she did this for many days; and when Paul was grieved, he turned to the spirit and said: "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out that same hour. But when her masters saw that the hope of their profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the forum to the magistrates, and brought them forward saying: "These men are disturbing our city, being Jews, and they preach a sect which it is not lawful for us to receive or practise, since we are Romans." And the whole crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates, having stripped off their tunics, ordered them to be beaten with rods. And when they had laid many blows on them, they cast them into prison, charging the keeper of the prison to guard them carefully. Having received such a charge, he put them into the innermost part of the prison and fastened their feet in the stocks. But about midnight, while Paul and Silas were praying and singing a hymn to God, the other prisoners heard them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and the doors were opened and all the bonds were loosed. The keeper of the prison awoke, and when he saw the doors of the prison open, he drew his sword to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had fled. But Paul cried out with a loud voice, saying: "Do yourself no harm; for we are all here." On hearing this the keeper of the prison called for a light and went in, and trembling fell down at the feet of Paul and Silas, and when he had brought them outside, he said: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" And they said: "Believe in God Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household." And they spoke the word of the Lord to him with all who were in his house. And taking them at that very hour of the night he washed [them] from their wounds, and he was baptised with all his household. And bringing them into his house he set a table, and feasted with his whole household, believing in the Lord.'

Therefore, just as that spirit of Python, on hearing the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, was at once driven out of its dwelling and stirred up the whole people of the city against the preachers of the majesty of the only Son of God, so those unclean spirits have stirred up you too, with your followers, against us, his servants. Do not doubt that you are driven by the same spirits by which those who rose against Paul and Silas were driven, when you see yourself thus made a persecutor of the religion of God. That crowd was one which had not yet believed in the only Son of God, and they were such for no other reason than that they were without the Spirit of God, as you too are proved to be. For that you cannot have the Holy Spirit unless you believe in the only Son of God is made plain by what this keeper of the prison did: though he was certainly one of that resisting people, yet after he believed, because he was now ruled by the Holy Spirit by whom Paul and Silas were ruled, he embraced nothing but holding to the way of those for whose sake he had seen the doors of the prison opened of their own accord. So you, who are now driven by a contrary spirit, unless you believe in the only Son of God as we also believe, can have in you nothing but the spirit of our adversary. For that keeper said to the glorious Paul and Silas: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" And they said: "Believe in our Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household." It is clear therefore that you are not saved, because you have not yet believed in the Lord Jesus. Nor can you assert that you have believed in him, since you are persecuting him. Or do you think that you are not persecuting him himself in us? If you are not persecuting him himself in us, how is it that he himself says to Saul: "Why do you persecute me? I am Jesus whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against the goad." What was Saul doing, that he should hear this from the Lord? Surely what you are doing; for he denied the only Son of God just as you deny him. For Paul, then a persecutor but afterwards one who began to suffer persecution, did not persecute the Christians because they believed as you believe, that there was [a time] when he was not, that he was made from nothing, and [denied] that he is the true Son, but certainly because they dared to confess the only Son of God, because the Christians declared that they believed that the eternity of the Father and the Son is one, that the Godhead is one, that the power in the Father and the Son is one. These things Paul abhorred, thinking the Christians were in error; but when he was enlightened by him whom he was denying, when he came to know [the truth] from the books of Moses and from all the volumes of the prophets, at once he began to defend the things he had been attacking, the very things, namely, which those whom he persecuted defended before he believed. For the rest, who was so senseless, as you Arians are, or as is Photinus of the people of Sirmium, who is truly called Scotinus, as to believe in a creature, in one who was [at a time] when he was not, in one who was created from nothing? It is evident therefore that all of you, not believing as the glorious Church believes, are led by a contrary spirit, from which contrary spirit you cannot be freed unless you believe that he is the true Son of God.

"The bishops," you say, "insult me." Why do we seem to you insulting? Surely because we say: "Why do you pretend to be a Christian? For you are seen to be an Arian, you are seen to be an enemy of the religion of God." Hence we seem abusive to you and yours. But look at what the most blessed apostle said, so that we bishops might act against you wolves: "You know from the first day on which I entered Asia how I was with you all the time, serving the Lord in all humility and with tears and trials, which befell me through the plots of the Jews; how I held back nothing of what was profitable, how I proclaimed to you and taught publicly and from house to house, testifying to Jews and Greeks repentance towards God and faith in our Lord Jesus. And now, behold, bound in the spirit I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will befall me there, except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me in Jerusalem. But I count my life of no value as dear to me, compared with finishing my course and the ministry of the word which I received from the Lord, to testify to Jews and Greeks the gospel of the grace of God. And now I know that you will see my face no more, all of you among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom of the Lord Jesus. Therefore I testify to you this day that I am clean of the blood of all, and I have not failed to preach the whole will of God. Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as bishops to rule the church of the Lord, which he acquired with his own blood. I know that after my departure grievous wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock; from among yourselves men will arise and speak perverse things, to draw disciples after them. Therefore keep watch, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease to warn each one of you with tears." Since you see that these are the apostle's commands, what do you bid me do, so as not to seem insulting to you? Surely you bid me be silent and allow you, one of those grievous wolves foretold, to rage in any way you like against the flock of God. We see you wolves, whom the Holy Spirit saw fit to foretell through the apostle, the vessel of election, attempting to seize the whole flock of God; and we, the bishops whom the Holy Spirit has appointed to rule the church of God, as the blessed apostle says, ought we to spare you, the wolf? Ought we to revere the diadem of your kingdom, your earring too and your bracelets? Ought we to honour your garments, which you reckon distinguished, and despise the Creator and Ruler of all things? Who is more foolish than you, that you say: "I, an emperor, suffer injury from Lucifer, from a needy man"? You do not deign to say "from a bishop", because you were recognised to be a wolf and deserved rejection. You thought I should be loaded with such ill-will that you asserted that a servant of God had been insulting to you, the emperor. If you think us abusive, hear what blessed Paul answered to the chief of the priests when he forbade [him] to preach the only Son of God. "Paul," says Scripture, "looking intently at the council, said: 'Men, brothers, I have lived in all good conscience before God up to this day.' And the chief of the priests, Ananias, commanded those standing by him to strike Paul on the mouth. Then Paul said to him: 'God will strike you, you whitewashed wall. And do you sit to judge me according to the law, and contrary to the law order me to be struck?'" Therefore, if the sacred law cannot judge blessed Paul insulting because he said this to an unjust judge, neither can you justly call me proud when I tell you the truth and what you are. You mark me down as guilty of insults; but I ask you to say to whom you can complain about me. If to God, how can you complain to him whom you do not know? How, when you are a stranger to his house? But if you complain to yourself, what will you do, a man who can in no way harm the servants of God? If you torture, we are healed the more; if you torment, we are refreshed the more; if you kill, we shall live the more.

Because I dare to call you the forerunner of the Antichrist, you call me abusive. If your deeds do not show you to be this, consider with great care also the book of the most holy prophet Daniel, and you will find yourself one of those foretold persecutors of the religion of God. "In the first year of Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans Daniel saw a dream, and the visions of his head on his bed, and he wrote down his dream: I, Daniel, was looking; and behold, the four winds of heaven were driving upon the great sea, and four beasts [came up] out of the sea, one surpassing another in size. The first was like a lioness and had wings. And it rose from the earth and stood on the feet of a man, and the heart of a man was given to it. And behold, another beast like a she-bear, and it stood on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth, between its teeth. And thus it was told: 'Arise, devour much flesh.' After this beast I was looking, and behold, another beast like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird upon it, and the beast had four heads, and power was given to it. After this I was looking, and behold, a fourth beast, terrible, astonishing and exceedingly strong; its iron teeth devoured and broke in pieces, and it trampled the rest with its feet. And this beast was greater than the other beasts which had been seen before, and it had ten horns. And I was gazing at its horns, and behold, another, smaller horn came up in the midst of them, and three of the horns which were before it were uprooted before it. And behold, eyes like the eyes of a man were in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things. I was looking until thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow and the hair of his head like clean wool, and his throne a flame of fire, its wheels burning fire. A river of fire shone before him; thousands of thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. He sat in judgement, and the books were opened. I was looking then, because of the sound of the great words which that horn was speaking, until the beast was slain and perished, and its body was given to be burned. And the kingdom of the other beasts was taken away, and length of life was given them until a time. I was looking in the vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he came to the Ancient of Days. He came forward and was presented to him, and to him was given kingdom and honour and dominion, and all peoples, tribes, tongues serve him, and his power is an everlasting power which will never pass away, and his dominion [and] kingdom will not be destroyed. My spirit shuddered within me, I, Daniel, and the vision of my head troubled me. And I approached one of those standing by and sought the truth from him about all these things. And he told me the truth and made known to me the interpretation of the words: 'These four great beasts: four kingdoms will arise on the earth, and the saints of the most high God will receive the kingdom and will hold it for ever.' And I inquired diligently about the fourth beast, which was exceedingly terrible beyond the other beasts. Its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze; it devoured and broke in pieces and trampled the rest with its feet. And about its ten horns which were on its head, and about the other horn which came up and struck out the first three horns, which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than the others. I was looking, and that horn made war with the saints and prevailed against them, until the Ancient of Days came, and gave judgement to the saints of the most high God, and the time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom. And he said: 'The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which will surpass all kingdoms and will devour the whole earth and trample it and cut it down. Its ten horns: ten kings will arise, and after them another will arise who will surpass in evils all who were before him, and he will bring low three, and will speak words against the most high God, and will wear out the saints of the most high God, and will think to change times and law, and it will be given into his hand until a time, times and half a time. And the judgement will sit and will take away [his] kingdom, to destroy and ruin [it] to the end; and the kingdom and the power and the greatness of the kings has been given to the saints of the most high God. And his kingdom is everlasting, and all will serve and obey him.'"

I ought indeed to have inserted only that part which shows from your deeds which of the beasts you resemble; but so that you might know that you will be in that Gehenna into which glorious Daniel reports that beast was cast, unless you correct yourself, and how those whom you persecute will reign for ever, placed in the kingdom of the Lord, so that you might take note of it, we have added all these things. Likewise I judged that the whole revelation should be applied to this end, so that you, at least by reading, could satisfy yourself that you tyrants, persecutors of the religion of God, have been called beasts. For I desire to clear myself before your conscience, infected with the poisons of the Arian dogma, before you who are not religious but a destroyer of religion, of being, as you claim, insulting because I call you a wild beast or a savage monster, since you see that you are so called, names being applied to you according to your deeds. For the rest, it is plain that you bear the likeness of that fourth beast, that you desire to fulfil the things which it was foretold that beast would fulfil. It is written of the Antichrist, whom you resemble or are judged to be yourself: ‘He will speak words against the most high Lord, and will wear out the saints of the most high God, and will think to change times and law, and it will be given into his hand.’ These things you have already done and are doing. For when you say, ‘The Son of God is not true God, but was made from nothing,’ you speak words against God. For since we Christians claim one divinity for the Father and his only Son, and you attack this defence of ours, asserting of the Son that he was [at a time] when he was not and that he was made from nothing, you certainly prove that you are either the Antichrist or at least his forerunner. Nor can you be understood to be anything other than either the forerunner of the Antichrist or the Antichrist, you who dare to call the apostolic and evangelical faith heretical and try to claim your blasphemy as the catholic faith. You feel that you suffer injury because you are called a beast by us; you are found thinking to change the faith, that is, so that we should not believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed, but you have laid down that one must believe as your fellow-damned Arius [believed]. And you say that you are not rightly called a beast, when the most holy prophet called you a beast because you were going to do these things? You are not less in unbelief, Constantius, than the Antichrist; for you do not cease devouring the servants of God with iron teeth. Why say more? The Antichrist will do nothing except that the only Son of God be denied; this is what your most unclean mind, fattened with folly, is doing.

But however much you rage, your times will pass, they will pass, and those [times] will come in which you will see yourself, unless you take thought for yourself, placed in that fiery river; you will then see those whom you persecute so hostilely because they are unwilling to perish with you, not in that place of torments where you will be, but with the holy angels, ever giving thanks and praises to God, while you are in that flaming liquid. I do not want you to wonder if glorious Daniel has marked you out as a beast, when blessed Paul too said of your associates the Cretans: ‘Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies’; and below: ‘For this reason rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith, not attending to Jewish fables and the commandments of men who turn themselves away from the truth.’ Hence we bishops are injurious to you, because we rebuke and reproach you for having dared to turn yourself away from the truth, for having wished, abandoning the commandments of God, to cling to the blasphemies and commandments of men, and finally for having taken up idolatry after abandoning God. Hence I seem to be your enemy, because I want you to walk according to the precept of the apostle and not according to the commandments of Arius and the Jews. Against these most just allegations of ours, seeing yourself overcome by the truth, you are accustomed to say: ‘The sacred Scriptures teach that one must be subject to kings and to all who live in high station; and do you dare to heap such great and such things on me, Lucifer?’ These [passages] you look at; those of this kind which order you to be honoured you understand; but those which order you to act you pretend not to know: those which warn you to obey the priests of the Lord, those which press upon you that you ought to show yourself one among all your fellow-servants, and not to call yourself superior to anyone, if you wish to be found a servant of God. ‘These things,’ says the blessed apostle to Titus, ‘speak and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you.’ If you are a Christian, since you too are one of those on whose account he said, ‘These things speak and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you,’ then surely you ought to listen to me when I reprove you with all authority, not despise me. You will be a Christian then, if you do not despise me when I exhort you to persevere as a Christian; but if you despise [me], you are found to be no longer among the Christians, because if you had been a Christian you would not have despised him whom God has ordained to instruct his people, and to whom the apostle said: ‘These things speak and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you.’ For what do I urge on you? Only that you not be a murderer, that you not persecute the house of God, that you cease to torture, proscribe, deport, shut up in prison, butcher, destroy in various ways and kill those whom you see to be Christians; that you cease, finally, to blaspheme the only Son of God, that you accept the apostolic faith which you call heretical, namely this faith of ours which the bishops at Nicaea drew up against you and all heretics; that you believe as we do and deign to reject the idolatry instituted through Arius your teacher, so that you proclaim yourself a Christian, not an Arian; that you cease to bring false charges against the priests of God. This is my reproof, this my rebuke. The apostle tells me to rebuke you with all authority, and you say, ‘Lucifer does me injury,’ and you do not say, ‘A priest of God admonishes and exhorts [me] according to the precepts [given] to priests, so that I may lead a life most acceptable to God.’

Now, because you say that we owe you obedience, know that we recognise ourselves as debtors in rendering obedience not to you alone but also to all who live in high station. For the apostle says: ‘Remind them to be subject to rulers and magistrates, obedient, ready for every good work, to blaspheme no one, not to be quarrelsome but modest, showing all gentleness to all men. For we too were once foolish and unbelieving, going astray, serving various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another; but when the kindness and humanity of God our Saviour shone forth, not from works of righteousness which we did, but according to his mercy he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal through the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us honourably through Jesus Christ our Saviour, so that, justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of life.’ He reminds [us], then, that we ought to be subject in good works, not in evil ones. If it is a good work to destroy an absent man, to kill one unheard who cries out to clear himself, to punish with you, setting aside all regard for mercy, one whom we know to be innocent; if it is a good work to deny the only Son of God, a work acceptable to God to desert the apostolic faith and take up the heretical, you would rightly say that I act against the admonitions of the sacred Scriptures. I add this, that the apostle made mention of those rulers and magistrates who had not yet believed in the only Son of God, so that they might be drawn to believe by our humility and gentleness and long patience in adversity and the greatest obedience in fitting matters. But if you, because you are emperor, pretending to be one of us, compel us to abandon God and take up idolatry, will we have to comply with you, lest the precepts of the apostle seem to have been neglected? And yet you, who pretend to be a Christian, try to make Christians what you yourself are, that is, apostates, you who are still foolish and unbelieving, remaining in your malice, in which the apostle says we too were before recognition [of the truth], before receiving the sacred faith. In what things were we to comply with you, except that we should do what was lawful? Or when you say, blasphemous murderer, ‘Kill those who believe in the only Son of God; be persecutors of his house with me; deny him with me; reject the apostolic faith; take up my heresy, of which I have been a lover with all the strength of my heart’ — who is more wretched than you, that he should not avoid you, should not flee you, knowing that you who urge these things are a temple of demons? Because you hear these things, you say, ‘I suffer injury from Lucifer, a wretched man’; and since [you are] emperor, that blasphemous, polluted speech of yours is not followed by: ‘I hear what I deserve from Lucifer, priest of the Lord.’

The vessel of election [says] to the Galatians: ‘I marvel,’ he says, ‘that you are so quickly being transferred from him who called you in grace to another gospel, which is not another, except that there are some who trouble you and wish to overturn the gospel of Christ. But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel to you other than [the one we preached], let him be anathema. As we said before, so now I say again: if anyone announces to you [a gospel] other than what you received, let him be anathema.’ And do you think that you can be declared by me to be anything other than anathema, when I find you preaching otherwise than the blessed apostles handed down? So when you hear from me that I hold you anathema for preaching otherwise than the apostles preached, if you call me insulting, you will be able to recognize that you are lying, if you carry anything of a man in you, since you see that I call you anathema for this reason, that the blessed apostle has already anathematized you. You declare me insulting because I call you foolish; but how can I rightly be called insulting by you, when it is evident that I speak the truth, that you are indeed foolish? For if the Galatians hear ‘O foolish Galatians’ from the blessed apostle, why do you think that you ought not to be called by the name of fool? For if they were called foolish because they had obeyed false brothers, because, attending to the suggestions of those fellow-serpents of yours, they had decided that they ought to keep the sabbaths and that circumcision was to be observed, how much more deservedly are you called foolish, who have become a denier of the only Son of God!
