Because I say to you: ‘Snatch yourself away from the rabid Arian dogs; grieve that by clinging to their malignant council you yourself have become a dog,’ you call me insolent; but perhaps you do not know that the deniers of the only Son of God have been called dogs, called fat bulls, called sons of iniquity, the seed of the adulterer and the harlot, sons of perdition and wicked seed. If it escapes you that you have been so called by God, hear him saying through Isaiah to your fellow-blasphemers the Jews: ‘Come here, sons of iniquity, seed of the adulterer and the harlot. In whom have you delighted, and against whom have you opened your mouth, and against whom have you let loose your tongue? Are you not sons of perdition, a wicked seed?’ And in another place: ‘See that all have been blinded, they have not known how to be wise; all are dumb dogs that cannot bark, dreaming in bed, loving to slumber. And they are shameless dogs, souls that know no fullness, and they are worthless, knowing no understanding; they have all followed their own ways.’ Who are these to whom, or on account of whom, these things are said? Surely those whom the only Son of God accuses in the twenty-first psalm by the mouth of David, saying: ‘Many calves have surrounded me, fat bulls have besieged me. They opened their mouth against me, like a lion ravening and roaring’; and below: ‘Many dogs have surrounded me, the council of the malignant has besieged me; they have pierced my hands and feet.’ So when you notice that those masters of yours in sacrilege have been called calves, fat bulls and dogs, you, one of the council of the malignant, will not be able to judge me insulting because I call you by the names by which your fellow-pestilences were and are called; for you are not less in wickedness, you who dare to say ‘there was [a time] when he was not, and he was made from nothing,’ that you should not be called by those names that fit you. But if you wish not to be called by these names, change your ways, correct your errors, as the most blessed Paul and others from that faithless people corrected [theirs]. Because I say to you, ‘Snatch yourself away from the council of the malignant,’ I seem to you insulting. On what account? Surely because I profess myself a Christian, because I have refused to abandon God and go after your idolatry. We are not the first to be called insulting and proud by you sacrilegious men; for all those too were so called who resisted the deadly edicts of your fellow-tyrants.

To pass over the others as well, at the close of my speech I shall turn again to King Antiochus alone. Did he judge those who resisted him insulting and proud, or not? Without doubt, since they thought them to have been insulting and proud, he persecuted those dedicated to God with such cruelty, even to death. It remains, then, for you to see what further Antiochus did beyond what you already know; and if you can rightly say that they were proud and insulting to Antiochus, you can [say it] of us too. For we suffer from you the things that they also endured from Antiochus; we cry out for the faith, for religion, just as they too cried out; we profess to serve the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, just as they too confessed. ‘The king,’ says Scripture, ‘sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers and of God, so as not to observe them, and also to defile the temple that was in Jerusalem and call it [the temple] of Olympian Jupiter, and [the one] on Gerizim, as befitted those who inhabited the place, [the temple] of Jupiter the Hospitable. And the onset of evils was most terrible and grievous to all. For the temple was full of the revels of the gentiles, of men whoring with harlots and approaching women in the holy precincts, and moreover bringing inside things that were not permitted; the altar too was full of unlawful things which were forbidden by the laws. Neither were the sabbaths kept nor the ancestral feast days observed.’ And below: ‘They were led by bitter compulsion every month on the day of the king’s birthday — it was pitiful; and when the rites of Liber were celebrated, they were compelled to go around for Liber wearing ivy. And a decree went out to the neighbouring cities of the Greeks, at the suggestion of the Ptolemies, to carry out the same practice against the Jews and to make them sacrifice, and to kill those who would not go over to the customs of the Greeks. So one could see the misery. For two women were brought in, charged with having circumcised their sons; they hung their infants at their breasts, and when they had led them publicly around the city, they threw them headlong from the wall. Others, who had run together into nearby caves and were secretly celebrating the seventh day, when this was reported, were burned, because they were afraid to bring help to themselves on the glorious holy day.’ What do you think the worshippers of God ought to have done then? Ought they to have pleased God or Antiochus? If you do not think they ought to have pleased Antiochus, then neither [ought] we [to please] you, since you too, though in another way, nevertheless desire to take us away from God and join us to the devil, as he wished [to do with] them. The same cruelty is carried out by you; [you are] just as savage and unjust towards those who resist your deadly edict. It remains, then, as has often been said, that you grieve that you have erred, and, recognizing that you are a murderer and a blasphemer, deserter of God, present yourself again to the house [of God]; otherwise you will have yourself to blame, when you begin to see yourself there where all those fellow-tyrants of yours now are.
